entry.title: New Semester Tablet Buying Guide | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. tip:
This article is only published on greataden.top. Please indicate the source when reprinting. Unless otherwise specified, the prices of all electronic products mentioned in this article are subject to the original prices on JD.com. Due to space limitations, this article only provides the most basic advice, the advantages and disadvantages of each company, and a price comparison. Subjective items such as screen and system user experience are not taken into account.
prefaceThe annual bushi is just around the corner, and as we all know, Heyi Meigao's ban on the use of electronic devices on campus is basically nonsense after just a few months of school, allowing everything except mobile phones to be used freely. As we all know, because textbooks are as heavy as bricks, many students tend to use tablets to read electronic textbooks and take class notes. The current electronics market is a mixed bag, with all sorts of brands rushing to make tablets (specifically Lenovo Xiaoxin, whose tablets are pure electronic garbage). So today, Heyi Meigao Hardware Society brings you a guide to buying tablets at different price points and for different needs now and in the next six months. FaithThere's a kind of mental disability called Apple, a kind of patriotism called Huawei, and an explosion called Samsung (bushi). Judging from the names, everyone knows who I'm criticizing. The first two are the ones I think definitely need to be carefully considered. The reason is simple: the closed system ecosystem means that you can almost only buy the complete set, as well as the high price and low cost-effectiveness (the latter two are especially relevant to Apple). To give a simple example: Suppose Zhang San buys an iPad air5 (256GB), then in order to take notes, he also needs a second-generation Apple Pencil and an official Apple Magic Control keyboard. The total original price of these three items on JD.com is 8550 RMB, which is now enough for a high-end computer mainframe. Moreover, once you buy a tablet, you must buy an iPhone and an Apple computer to achieve the best ecosystem synergy and maximum efficiency (I can write a separate article about why later). The iPhone 13 Pro 256G version is priced at 8200 on JD.com, the M1 version of the MacBook Air 13 is 7400, and the M2 version is 9200. A complete set would cost at least two thousand yuan. Forgive my bluntness, whoever buys it is an idiot (just ignore the fact that my family is so poor they only have money left). Huawei's situation is similar, but in fact, Huawei's most important problem does not lie here, but in other aspects, which I will introduce in detail below. Apple EditionOnce you've made up your mind to put up with Apple's poor software compatibility and game isolation on your computer, please read on. Alternatively, you can choose to jump to the Huawei section. First, let me state my personal opinion: I won't buy pro unless it's necessary. The difference between the iPad air and iPad pro isn't that significant for the average consumer!ipad air Whether it's performance or user experience, it's hard to truly appreciate it without using an iPad for video editing. The same applies to gaming; the same M1 chip can completely handle the current performance killer, Genshin Impact. Taking notes goes without saying. To be honest, Apple really doesn't have much to say about it. It has a solid screen and stylus quality, a smooth system, and a whole host of other advantages. The only problem is its price. If you don't play games and won't need very specialized software for your college major in the future, but just want to use it for reading, writing, and taking notes, and your budget is not limited, then the Apple family bucket is indeed a good choice. Finally, when buying Apple products, please remember: Buy what you need, don't create demand. Beware of Cook's knife technique [doge] Huawei EditionActually, I didn't originally want to include Huawei in the discussion, but since many people only know about Huawei besides Apple, I'll bring it up anyway. One thing is clear: HarmonyOS is not a user-friendly "mobile phone" system; its real advantage lies in the Internet of Everything. Never buy Huawei just because of HarmonyOS; its advantages may not be apparent for the next five years. Moreover, the desktop mode of the HarmonyOS system (the mode in which tablets improve the mouse and keyboard user experience by imitating the computer interface) is very poorly designed, almost unusable. Then comes a common misconception: the so-called "support for domestic products". Huawei has never been a conscientious company. Admittedly, Huawei is awesome, truly awesome. It is one of only four mobile phone manufacturers in the world that can design its own chips, and it has also modified Android to develop its own HarmonyOS system. However, it's really not as good as most people imagine. The Enjoy series is a huge rip-off for the poor, with the best configuration in the same price range coupled with the highest price. After being sanctioned, prices skyrocketed, with the P50E 778G chip selling for 4,000 yuan (compared to 2,000 yuan for the same Xiaomi configuration). Back when Huawei was still using Android 10's EMUI, it blatantly violated Google's Android Open Source Convention by blocking bl and root channels. (If anyone criticizes me for worshipping foreign things, please take a look up. I also criticize Apple, much harsher than Huawei.) In short, Huawei is indeed facing difficulties, but its current products offer very low cost-effectiveness. As consumers, especially those with limited budgets, the primary consideration should be whether their products are worth their investment, rather than whether they support so-called national enterprises and patriotism. Next, we'll begin the official Huawei tablet recommendation. If you only want to do light office work and study, the MatePad 11 (3999 + 600 + 450) is a good option.matepad11 If you want to play some games, you'll need Pro 2021 (3299 + 600 + 450).matepad pro Samsung EditionSamsung's newly released tab s8 series tablets this year (s8 4500-5700+700, s8+ 5700-7000+700, s8 ultra 7900-8900+700) call themselves the "King of Android Tablets." Although I still have doubts about whether this lousy 8-for-1 chip can be worthy of the King of Tablets, it must be said that Samsung is currently the most powerful manufacturer deeply involved in styluses. Samsung's first stylus was the one that came with the note1 11 years ago. Eleven years have passed since then, and its technological accumulation is not something that other manufacturers can easily catch up with. Based on my own experience, I believe that Samsung's note-taking experience is on par with Apple's and slightly surpasses Apple's. One of Samsung's notable features is its DEX mode. Samsung does a pretty good job with this computer mode. Personally, I was forced to use a tablet to work because my computer broke down, but now I haven't turned it on for two months. In terms of performance, the new generation Snapdragon 8 is quite good, but it gets very hot... (I personally tested it; this article was typed using a Samsung tab s8 with an external mechanical keyboard.) Samsung tab s8The looks are alright too (in my personal opinion). Finally, a purchase recommendation: The difference between the s8 series products is almost only in screen size. The stylus of the s8+/ultra has a very slight improvement over the s8 (6ms-2.8ms). Because it's a near-native system, it can be paired with any Android phone (though the user experience isn't very good either). If you have a limited budget, you can buy the base model s8 (which I am currently using), but based on my own experience, I recommend the s8+. Meanwhile, there are reports that Samsung is about to launch the s8FE, which will use the Snapdragon 8+Gen1 chip. If you can afford to wait, you should definitely wait! The difference between these two chips is stark. Summary of the products in the Faith section above: Choose wisely and avoid falling into traps, but the price is not worthwhile, and it is worth considering if you have a very sufficient budget. Cost-effectivenessHaving discussed high-end tablets, let's move on to the mid-to-low-end market. Unlike the hidden struggle in the high-end market, the mid-to-low-end market is truly "like water and fire". Xiaomi, OPPO, VIVO, Honor, as well as Apple's digital series and Huawei's low-end series are fiercely competing here. Next, we will introduce them one by one. Xiaomi EditionThe top contender is the Xiaomi Mi Tablet 5/5 pro (1999~2499 +350+400). As a tablet with a stylus latency of 22ms (Samsung's industry-leading 2.8ms, most others are between 6-9ms, and the sensation is generally not noticeable below 10ms), it can be ruled out as a learning tablet. At the same time, MIUI for pad cannot be said to be particularly good. Although the performance of the Xiaolong 860/870 combined with its price provides an excellent daily entertainment and gaming experience, the most important use of tablets in this article is for learning. Therefore, the Xiaomi pad 5 is not recommended for purchase.Xiaomi Tablet 5 However, there are reports that the Xiaomi Mi Pad 6 has effectively improved the above problems. Patient students can wait until the first half of the year, as it might be a very cost-effective option. OPPOThe second contender is OPPO's first tablet, the OPPO pad (2200~3000 +350+500). As the first tablet from a green factory, OPPO has shown great sincerity. Whether it is the 2k high refresh rate, the large battery or the LCD eye-protecting screen, it is basically on par with other mainstream tablet manufacturers. Although the stylus latency reached 16ms due to lack of experience, and the keyboard is not magnetically charged but has a built-in battery, resulting in an overall thickness, considering its price... it's not impossible to use. If you are currently using a new OPPO phone released in the last two years, then the OPPO pad can be considered one of your high-quality choices. OPPO pad However, please note: OPPO also has another, even lower-priced OPPO pad air. In my opinion, it's pure electronic garbage. It can only play iQiyi and games, so it's not included in the recommended list. vivoThe third place winner is the vivo pad (2500~3000 +350+600). The blue manufacturer followed the green manufacturer into the pad market this year, but its performance can only be described as less than satisfactory. Although its basic specifications and price are roughly the same as the O-board, it falls short in terms of the stylus, which most affects the learning experience, with a latency of 17.5ms. non-magnetic chargingTherefore, its stylus is relatively heavier and thicker. The fact that I need to replace the battery myself makes me list it and the Xiaomi tablet's stylus as unusable, so overall I don't recommend buying it. vivo pad Apple's low-end versionThe fourth place goes to a heavyweight player: the iPad 2021, also known as the iPad 9 (2500~3700 +730). As a player in Apple's digital series, which focuses on the low-end market, I have to say it's very tempting. Its powerful processor and screen, which are almost identical to the air Pro, make it an excellent tablet for "audio-visual entertainment". iPad 9 Attentive students should have noticed that I didn't mention its learning experience. That's right, the learning experience on this tablet can't be described as good; it's practically unusable. First, it doesn't have an official magnetic keyboard; you can only choose to use an external third-party keyboard or type on the screen, which directly eliminates productivity queues.Secondly, it uses the first-generation iPad pencil, which cannot magnetically charge, and its charging method is bizarre, comparable to an Apple mouse, resulting in poor latency (due to Apple's manipulation, I couldn't find the latency parameters for the high-end Apple pencil 1, but according to reviews, it should be around 20ms).Finally, it's really ugly (personal opinion, light criticism). In summary, it is basically classified as a Mi-board 5, and V-boards are not recommended for purchase. Huawei Low-EndThe fifth contestant is arguably in the same heavyweight class as the Apple I just took away: the Huawei M6 tablet (1600~2300 +0). Why is the price +0? Because it does not support stylus, nor does it support the official magnetic keyboard. Isn't that outrageous? The mold is from three years ago, and the chip is from Kirin 980 inventory. This can sell for the same or even higher price as Xiaomi tablets. It has to be said that Huawei really has a knack for ripping off the poor. Huawei Tablet M6 My Samsung tab s3 from four or five years ago looks better than him. (Personal opinion, you can also find it beautiful) Similar to the V-board, Guozi low-end, and Mi5, it is classified as a non-recommended purchase. ##Glory EditionSixth place, and the last player in the low-to-mid-range category, is the Honor Tablet v7 Pro. Honor Tablet V7 Pro It must be said that the Honor tablet is deeply inherited from its father, Huawei. Although it bypasses sanctions, it does not affect the fact that the processor is extremely bad. Whether it is the MediaTek 1300T in the V7 Pro or the Snapdragon 680 in the Honor tablet 8, it can only be said to be limited to daily learning and light gaming. However, its stylus experience seems to be quite good. Although I have doubts about its 2ms advertising, it is definitely not much different, and it is still very good for taking notes. If you happen to own a recent Honor phone but don't play games much, then the Honor Tablet V7 Pro would be the perfect choice. Special Tablet EditionAlthough the tablet positioning of various companies generally follows the standards of mid-to-low-end and high-end product lines, there will always be a few exceptions. For example Savior Y700 Savior Y700 Placing this tablet here has absolutely no recommendation whatsoever; it's just a reminder to students who are thinking of buying a gaming tablet and still being able to study. It really can only play games... They don't even have styluses; the official refusal to become a productive force is a fact. There's another one to send.Shin-chan pad Pro 2021 Shin-chan pad Pro 2021 It has to be said that Lenovo is truly a place full of eccentricities. The biggest problem with this guy is probably the stylus, which is basically unusable. With that garbage system, it's practically paying for suffering. These two are highly, highly not recommended. Then there's a truly unique trend: "tablets, but not completely flat products." Microsoft surface surface Pro 8 This is also a non-recommended purchase level; it's not that it doesn't work well, but rather that it's unsuitable. The essence of the surface is still a computer, just a very portable computer. The touch experience of Windows has always been terrible, and even after the Windows 11 upgrade, it is only usable. It's pretty good for office work. Some teachers at American high schools (yes, I'm talking about cr) use Surfaces, but they're not suitable for taking notes. OneNote isn't a good note-taking software. Finally, let me summarize.High-end recommendations: Samsung tab s8+ and the upcoming s8FE version. Those with a large budget can also choose Apple or Huawei based on their own circumstances. Highly recommended mid-to-low-end products: OPPO pad, Honor V7 Pro We do not recommend purchasing: Xiaomi Tablet 5/5 Pro, Huawei M6, iPad 9, Legion Y700, Lenovo Xiaoxin Pro 11, or the entire surface series. In conclusion: Thanks to ZOL (Zhongguancun Online) and JD.com for providing parameters, images, and price data.

entry.title: My personal opinion on the Lenovo Xiaoxin series low-temperature tin incident | Aden's Space
entry.url: /en/2023/02/27/关于联想小新系列低温锡事件个人看法/
entry.content:
Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. tip:
This article is only published on greataden.top. Please indicate the source when reprinting. As these are personal opinions, the author is not legally responsible for any negative statements appearing in the article.
prefaceAs the matter escalated, on February 13, Lenovo's official Xiaoxin Weibo account responded to the incident with an article titled "Xiaoxin Light and Thin Notebook Low-Temperature Solder Paste Soldering Technology Description" (hereinafter referred to as the "Description"). The document stated that low-temperature solder paste soldering is a mature and more environmentally friendly technology for electronic product production lines that meets national and international standards. It also indicated that, based on after-sales data from Xiaoxin Light and Thin Notebooks over the years, there is no difference in repair rates between models using low-temperature solder paste soldering technology and models using room-temperature solder soldering technology. FirstI myself use a Lenovo Xiaoxin computer. I bought it from JD.com's self-operated flagship store in November last year (2022). The model is Xiaoxin 14 PRO-IAH5R, and the price is 6199 (I personally feel that this price is reasonable). My first impression of it is that it is light, too light. According to official data, the 14Pro weighs 1.3kg, roughly the same as the weight of the 2020 MacBook Air. Even with a 100W gallium nitride charger, its portability and thinness are beyond doubt. SecondlyRegarding this low-temperature tin incident, I do not believe it is part of Lenovo's planned scrapping. After watching the video of a laptop repair guy on Bilibili (I'm a fan of his), I found that most of the problems were with AMD platform machines. As is well known, AMD is notoriously hot, and some of the machines that undergo empty soldering are caused by high-temperature desoldering of on-board memory. This may be due to the unreasonable design of the heat dissipation structure at the time. Among the Intel models affected, I analyzed that it was because Lenovo used too much vinyl, which caused the CPU to be fixed. When the motherboard deformed due to the shaking of the computer, the CPU could not move, causing the solder ball to be misaligned. So this gives us a lesson:Don't shake your computer unless necessary. Be careful to hold it firmly.。 Therefore, I believe it is a design flaw. in the endWhat if it happens to you? My advice is to try not to contact Lenovo after-sales service. In the two months since I bought it, I've realized that Lenovo's after-sales service is exceptionally poor. I can say that some of the after-sales engineers' understanding of computers and their problem-solving methods are not even as good as some of my classmates. So, if you encounter this problem, it seems you can get it repaired for free under warranty (?). If it's out of warranty, go find a repair technician you're familiar with in a computer store. They might only charge a labor fee to resolder the unsoldered parts. Lenovo's after-sales service will directly replace the motherboard for you.I need 1000Then the price would be a bit high. In conclusion, I do not believe that the "low-temperature tin incident" was part of Lenovo's planned scrapping; it may simply be caused by a design flaw. Secondly, to avoid these problems as much as possible, you'd better hold on tight. Finally, if you get scammed, just go through the warranty and find a repairman to fix it. There's really no need to send it to official after-sales service (waves).

entry.title: Honor Magic5 Series Launched | Aden's Space
entry.content: Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. Review of the Honor Magic5 series The Honor Magic5 series is a flagship phone released by Honor on March 6, 2023, including two models: the Honor Magic5 and the Honor Magic5 Pro. Both phones are equipped with the new Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 processor, an OLED screen that supports a 120Hz refresh rate, and a rear camera with a three-body star ring design. So, what's the difference between them? Which one is more suitable for you? Let's compare them. First, in terms of appearance, both the Honor Magic5 and Magic5 Pro feature a quad-curved screen design, but the screen size and resolution differ. The Honor Magic5 has a 6.73-inch screen with a resolution of 2688×1224 pixels, while the Honor Magic5 Pro has a 6.81-inch screen with a resolution of 2848×1312 pixels. Both support 1.07 billion color displays and a wide DCI-P3 color gamut, but in terms of peak brightness, the Honor Magic5 Pro is higher, reaching 1800 nits, while the Honor Magic5 is 1600 nits. In addition, the Honor Magic5 Pro also supports LTPO technology, which can adaptively adjust the refresh rate according to the content, saving battery power while ensuring smoothness. Secondly, in terms of performance, the Honor Magic5 series all use the Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 processor, which is an SoC chip based on the 4nm process, with powerful computing power, graphics processing capabilities and AI performance. Both are equipped with a combination of LPDDR5X memory and UFS 4.0 flash memory, and offer two storage capacity options: 256GB and 512GB. However, in terms of memory, the Honor Magic5 is only available in 8GB and 12GB specifications, while the Honor Magic5 Pro has a top-of-the-line version with 16GB. In addition, the Honor Magic5 Pro is exclusively equipped with a Display Chip that can assist the processor in tasks such as graphics rendering and video encoding and decoding. Secondly, in terms of photography, the Honor Magic5 series all adopts a three-body star ring design rear camera module and has the same configuration: a 50-megapixel wide-angle main camera + a 122° ultra-wide-angle lens + a high-definition macro lens. This camera system can achieve multiple shooting modes and effects, and supports HDR10+ video recording. Regarding the front-facing camera, there are some differences: the Honor Magic5 uses a 42-megapixel single-camera solution, and both the internal and external screens are equipped with front-facing cameras; The Honor Magic5 Pro uses a 50-megapixel dual-camera design and only has a front-facing camera on the internal screen. Finally, in terms of battery life, although both phones use a 4750mAh (typical) battery capacity and support 66W Super Fast Charging technology (requiring the original charger and data cable), there may be differences in battery life performance in actual use due to factors such as screen size, resolution, and refresh rate. The specific circumstances depend on individual usage habits and scenarios.

entry.title: Honor Qinghai Lake & Solid-State Battery Technology | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. Honor Magic5 series "Qinghai Lake" battery technologyThe Honor Magic5 is a highly anticipated smartphone that has recently sparked widespread discussion because it features a new battery technology known as "Qinghai Lake Battery Technology". Qinghai Lake is China's largest inland saltwater lake and one of the highest lakes in the world. Due to its high altitude, dry and cold climate, the lake water contains a large amount of beneficial elements such as lithium and magnesium. The Honor Magic5's battery technology utilizes these elements to improve battery performance and lifespan. Specifically, Qinghai Lake battery technology uses lithium-magnesium-silicon (LMS) material, a new type of battery material that has higher energy density and longer lifespan than traditional lithium-ion batteries. This material can not only increase battery capacity, but also improve the battery's fast charging capacity and stability, while reducing the battery's volume and weight. In addition, the Honor Magic5 also adopts intelligent temperature control technology, which can adjust the battery temperature in a timely manner during use to prevent overheating and overdischarge, thereby ensuring the safety and stability of the battery. The advantages of Qinghai Lake battery technology lie in its sustainability and environmental friendliness. The material resources of this technology come from nature and have the potential for recycling. In addition, this technology can reduce the impact of battery waste on the environment, which is beneficial to environmental protection and sustainable development. Overall, the Honor Magic5's Qinghai Lake battery technology is an exciting innovation that not only improves battery performance and lifespan, but also has environmental and sustainable advantages. It is believed that in the future, this new battery technology will be more widely used, bringing new opportunities for the development of smartphones and other electronic devices. Solid-state battery technology in mobile phonesWith the development of smartphones, battery life has become an increasingly important issue. To meet users' demand for long battery life, mobile phone manufacturers have been exploring new battery technologies. Among them, solid-state battery technology has attracted much attention. Solid-state battery technology is a new type of battery technology. Its main feature is that it uses solid electrolytes instead of traditional liquid electrolytes. Compared to traditional batteries, solid-state batteries have higher energy density, longer lifespan, and safer characteristics. At the same time, it can significantly reduce the volume and weight of the battery. Compared to traditional batteries, solid-state batteries have the following advantages:
Higher energy density. Solid-state batteries have a higher energy density than traditional batteries because they use more efficient materials and a tighter structure. Longer lifespan. Solid-state batteries are less prone to problems such as battery swelling and evaporation of liquid electrolytes, and therefore can maintain efficient and stable performance for a longer period of time. Safer. Because solid-state electrolytes are stable solids, solid-state batteries are safer under extreme conditions such as high temperatures, short circuits, overcharging, and overdischarging. Less volume and weight. Since solid-state batteries do not require liquid electrolytes and leak-proof structures, smaller and lighter batteries can be designed.
Solid-state battery technology has very broad application prospects, and can be used not only in smartphones, but also in other electronic devices and electric vehicles. Currently, some manufacturers have begun developing solid-state battery technology and have achieved some encouraging results in the laboratory. However, solid-state battery technology still faces some challenges, such as high manufacturing costs and difficult production. Therefore, a great deal of research and development is still needed in the future to enable this technology to be widely applied to the market.

This sensor combination allows the Find X6 to take stunning photos in any lighting conditions. The main sensor is capable of capturing incredible detail in bright and low-light environments. The ultra-wide-angle sensor is great for landscapes and group photos, while the telephoto sensor lets you zoom in on distant objects without losing detail. The Find X6 also has a number of impressive camera features, including:

screen The OPPO Find X6 also features a stunning display. It has a 6.7-inch AMOLED display with a resolution of 1440 x 3120 pixels. Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 processor: This powerful processor ensures that the Find X6 can handle the most demanding tasks. 12GB of RAM: This ensures that the Find X6 can multitask smoothly. 256GB of storage: This gives you enough space to store your photos, videos, and apps. Overall, the OPPO Find X6 is an excellent smartphone, perfect for photography enthusiasts. It has a powerful camera system, a stunning display, a long-lasting battery, and many other impressive features. entry.title: On stratification | Aden's Space
entry.content: Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. On stratificationintroduction (to a piece of writing)The essence of differentiated teaching should be to teach students of different levels and levels separately in order to achieve...efficiencyofmaximize。 And based on school grades,Standardized examinationGrades andIndividual examination scheduleIt's up to the teacher to decide, not just based on performance and grades. In terms of the efficiency of education and teaching, what is suitable for students is the best. Blindly before the teacher understands the students' arrangementsBased solely on grades and performanceLayering islow efficiency、No effectYes. Scenario reproductionThe school I attend is an American curriculum high school. When we were in our second year of high school, the school implemented a "tiered" system. The original intention of tiered instruction was to provide more efficient and targeted teaching. In the first tiering, I was assigned to the third tier (we studied the SAT in the first tier, and the SAT and TOEFL in the second, but currently we mainly study the collections series, and the third tier is studying the TOEFL). My grades were not outstanding. I did not achieve my ideal score or the standards for studying the SAT in the last exam. However, due to the timely submission of assignments and acceptable class performance, based on the school GPA and some TOEFL scores (the teacher said GPA was 40%, TOEFL was 60%, but this is obviously...).Unreliable(Otherwise, my classmates' TOEFL scores would be too bad) They stratified me and placed me in the second tier. According to my own considerations and plan, my study schedule is to start studying SAT-related courses during the summer vacation. I have taken the TOEFL exam about twice before, so I should focus on preparing for TOEFL-related content during this period. Furthermore, the upcoming AP course in May will take up my spare time practicing for the TOEFL, and I will need...More time at schoolLet's practice for the TOEFL. So I contacted the principal and the grade director to inquire about how to keep it on the current floor. Initially, I received their advice, but in the end, they agreed.SupportMy personal choice (I had previously contacted my current teacher and received the same information).Support）。 When I went to my newly assigned teacher to sign the application form this morning, as instructed by the grade director, what I received was...tough、negativeThe reason given in response was: "If I sign for you, more and more classmates will ask me to sign, so the stratification will be meaningless." I now feel that this stratification is just...surface workBecause the teacher didn't genuinely consider your learning schedule when approving or rejecting your application, but instead rejected it solely based on the "difficulty of the job," this kind of differentiated teaching behavior would be...low efficiency、MeaninglessThis will severely impact my schedule for subsequent standardized exams, potentially affecting my upcoming AP and TOEFL exams.score。 When I discussed this matter with the grade director last night, he promised that he would call the two teachers over for morning self-study to discuss it together. However, the truth is, he will do so.important、DecisiveIf things are delayedDragAlthough I contacted him to remind him several times, he still didn't take any action by the deadline. The principal's reply also suggested that I contact the grade director/homeroom teacher (the same teacher in our class) to resolve the issue. I realized how inefficient it was to resolve such a simple yet important matter in such a school. This made me question the efficiency and methods of implementing other administrative matters in the school, and thus the authenticity of students' college entrance examinations in previous years. SubsequentWhen I went to my homeroom teacher/grade leader again this morning to seek his help in solving the problem, I was told that I needed to solve it myself. Before thatPromiseThe help they provided me was not entirelyInvalidYes? My opinion is that it's better not to mention it at all. In the afternoon, when I went to the new teacher to resolve this issue again, the procedures mentioned earlier were complete.Change and changeNow, such a simple thing will be completely...complicationThat's it. I was required to write a clear explanation of the situation, and the teacher in my previous class was also required to write a clear evaluation. They also asked me to set a target score that I must reach by the end of the semester. There must be a very formal paper statement (voice-over: the paper "application" I wrote this morning is invalid), and I must be informed before the procedures are completed.Cannot leaveThe second floor. So if we follow this process, if I want to stay at this level from now on...Should I take the initiative to lower my school grades?What I can't understand is, can't I "not go up"? After this incident, I deeply realized the administrative efficiency of such a school.soofLowTo make things as simple as possiblecomplicationThis kind of issue, which only involves teaching arrangements, is actually...It cannot be resolved through the principal.This requires us to coordinate independently, which reflects the principal's and grade director's...Inaction、Get rid of responsibility。 At such a school, I couldn't help but question the good college entrance examination results of the previous few years.inefficient、InactionHow do schools gain access to prestigious universities around the world?favorof

entry.title: Honor 90 Series Review | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. Honor 90 series phone review: 200-megapixel main camera, 3840Hz high-frequency PWM dimming screen, combining thinness and battery life.The Honor 90 series is Honor's latest flagship phone, officially released on May 29, 2023. The Honor 90 series phones come in two models: the Honor 90 and the Honor 90 Pro. Their main features are a 200-megapixel photo camera, a zero-risk dimming eye-protecting screen, a 5000mAh lightweight and long battery life, and the powerful performance of the Snapdragon 7 and Snapdragon 8+ Gen1 chips. So, what are the differences between these two phones? How do they stand out in the competition at the same price point? This article will provide a detailed introduction and comparison of the various configurations of the Honor 90 and Honor 90 Pro phones, covering aspects such as design, display, core performance, camera, battery life, and charging, to help you make a more informed purchasing decision. Appearance designThe Honor 90 and Honor 90 Pro showcase distinctive features in their exterior design. The front of the Honor 90 features a curved screen with a centered hole. This hole is relatively small and located in the center of the top of the screen, giving it a simple and smooth feel. The "figure-eight" camera module design on the back adds a unique touch to the overall look. The Honor 90 also supports NFC, making it convenient for users to perform near-field communication. The device is relatively thin and light, weighing 183g and 7.8mm thick, making it more comfortable to hold and easier to operate. image In contrast, the front of the Honor 90 Pro features a pill-shaped punch-out curved screen. This punch-out design is relatively large and located in the center of the top of the screen, giving it a unique sense of technology. The "figure-eight" camera module design on the back is basically the same as that of the Honor 90, showcasing the brand's consistent style. Like the Honor 90, the Honor 90 Pro also supports NFC, making it convenient for users' daily use. However, the Honor 90 Pro is relatively heavy, weighing 192g and 8.1mm thick, which may feel slightly heavy when held in the hand. image display screenBoth the Honor 90 and Honor 90 Pro use OLED technology in terms of displays, providing an excellent visual experience. The Honor 90 features a 6.7-inch screen with a resolution of 2664x1200 pixels, ensuring a detailed display. Meanwhile, the Honor 90's screen also boasts an impressive 120Hz refresh rate, adding a sense of realism to the smooth sliding and animation effects. The peak brightness of up to 1600 nits makes the Honor 90 clearly visible even in bright environments. In addition, it uses 3840Hz high-frequency PWM dimming technology to provide a more comfortable visual experience. image The Honor 90 Pro is equipped with a larger 6.78-inch screen with a resolution of 2700x1224 pixels, presenting more detailed picture details. Like the Honor 90, the Honor 90 Pro also features a 120Hz refresh rate and a peak brightness of 1600 nits, bringing users a smooth and clear visual experience. Similarly, it also uses 3840Hz high-frequency PWM dimming technology to provide more comfortable screen brightness adjustment. image core performanceThe Honor 90 and Honor 90 Pro have significant differences in core performance. The Honor 90 is equipped with the Snapdragon 7 Gen1 chip, which is a mid-range chip based on the 6nm process. It has 4 A78 large cores and 4 A55 small cores, with a maximum clock speed of 2.4GHz and an Adreno 642L GPU. While this chip's performance is not weak, it is not outstanding either, and it does not have a significant advantage in the competition at the same price point. The Honor 90 has 8GB or 12GB of RAM and 128GB or 256GB of storage, and supports the UFS 3.1 standard. image The Honor 90 Pro is equipped with the Snapdragon 8+ Gen1 chip, which is a high-end chip based on the 5nm process. It has one A78 ultra-large core, three A78 large cores and four A55 small cores, with a maximum clock speed of 2.84GHz and an Adreno 660 GPU. This chip has very powerful performance and a clear advantage in the competition at the same price point. The Honor 90 Pro has 12GB of RAM and 256GB or 512GB of storage, and also supports the UFS 3.1 standard. image These parameters show that the Honor 90 Pro is much more powerful than the Honor 90 in terms of core performance, with obvious advantages in terms of processor, RAM, and storage. If you are a user with high requirements for phone performance, then the Honor 90 Pro is undoubtedly a better choice. CameraThe Honor 90 and Honor 90 Pro also have different camera configurations. The Honor 90 features a quad-camera rear design: a 200-megapixel main camera, an 8-megapixel ultra-wide-angle camera, a 2-megapixel macro camera, and a 2-megapixel depth-of-field camera. The 200-megapixel main camera uses a Sony IMX800 sensor, supports 9-in-1 pixel merging technology, and can output high-quality photos of 22.56 megapixels. The 8-megapixel ultra-wide-angle camera supports a 123° ultra-wide-angle field of view, allowing you to capture a wider range of landscapes. The 2-megapixel macro camera supports 4cm close-up focus and can photograph subtle objects. A 2-megapixel depth-of-field camera can provide better background blur. image The Honor 90 Pro features a five-camera rear setup: a 200-megapixel main camera, a 32-megapixel telephoto camera, an 8-megapixel ultra-wide-angle camera, a 2-megapixel macro camera, and a 2-megapixel depth-of-field camera. The 200-megapixel main camera is the same as the Honor 90, both using a Sony IMX800 sensor. The 32-megapixel telephoto camera is a major highlight of the Honor 90 Pro. It supports 2.5x optical zoom, 10x hybrid zoom, and 100x digital zoom, and has optical image stabilization, allowing you to photograph distant objects. The 8-megapixel ultra-wide-angle camera is the same as the Honor 90, and both support a 123° ultra-wide-angle field of view. The 2-megapixel macro camera and 2-megapixel depth-of-field camera are also the same as those in the Honor 90. image These parameters show that the Honor 90 Pro is more powerful than the Honor 90 in terms of camera, with better performance in both the main camera, telephoto lens, and ultra-wide-angle lens. If you are a user with high requirements for mobile phone photography, then the Honor 90 Pro is undoubtedly a better choice. Range and chargingThe Honor 90 and Honor 90 Pro also have different performances in terms of battery life and charging. The Honor 90 is equipped with a large-capacity 5000mAh battery, which can maintain a battery life of more than a day under light use and about half a day² under heavy use. In addition, the Honor 90 also supports 66W wired fast charging technology, which can fully charge the battery in 35 minutes. image The Honor 90 Pro is also equipped with a large-capacity 5000mAh battery, which is basically equivalent to the Honor 90 in terms of battery life. However, the Honor 90 Pro is faster than the Honor 90 in terms of charging speed. It supports 90W wired fast charging technology and can fully charge the battery in 28 minutes. image These parameters show that there is not much difference between the Honor 90 and Honor 90 Pro in terms of battery life. Both have a large-capacity 5000mAh battery and have good power consumption control capabilities. However, in terms of charging speed, the Honor 90 Pro is faster than the Honor 90 and comes with a 100W charger². sum upBy comparing the above aspects, we can see that the Honor 90 and Honor 90 Pro each have their own advantages and disadvantages. If you have high requirements for your phone's performance, camera, and charging speed, and don't mind a slightly heavier body and a larger, more prominent punch-hole screen design, then you can choose to buy the Honor 90 Pro. If you have high requirements for your phone's performance, camera, and charging speed, and don't mind a slightly heavier body and a larger, more prominent punch-hole screen design, then you can choose to buy the Honor 90 Pro. If you don't have high requirements for your phone's performance, camera, or charging speed, but prefer a thinner and lighter body and a smaller, more discreet punch-hole screen design, then you can choose to buy the Honor 90. Of course, regardless of which model you choose, you can enjoy the biggest highlight of the Honor 90 series – the 3840Hz high-frequency PWM dimming screen. This is currently the only phone on the market with this technology, which can provide you with a more comfortable visual experience. In conclusion, the Honor 90 series is a mobile phone with an innovative spirit and strong performance, which performs well in terms of appearance design, display, core performance, camera, battery life and charging. If you are looking for a phone that can meet your daily needs while bringing you surprises and fun, then the Honor 90 series is worth considering and buying.
I hope you like it. If you have any comments or suggestions about my article, please leave a comment below to let me know. Nubia Z50S Pro: An all-round flagship for flat-screen imaging, creating the art of light and shadow.The Nubia Z50S Pro is Nubia's latest flagship flat-screen imaging phone, officially released on July 20, 2023. In terms of imaging module design, the Nubia Z50S Pro pays homage to classic professional cameras, adopting a humanistic eye design. Computational Photography Upgrade: Humanistic Street Shooting 2.0 - Faster, More Powerful, and More ComprehensiveCustomized optics is the foundation of imaging hardware, while computational photography is the sublimation of software. With custom slide buttons, users can quickly launch street photography mode and easily capture wonderful moments with the help of the new Lightning Snapshot 4.0. Drawing inspiration from professional cameras, the Nubia Z50S Pro adds a surround photography feature, allowing users to obtain three images with different parameters in just one shot. The new Night Xiao Algorithm 2.0 and Galaxy Super Night 2.0 further optimize night scene shooting and starry sky photography, resulting in more delicate and clear low-light images. Nubia's optical super-resolution algorithm improves the sharpness of telephoto lenses by 30%. The new UI incorporates nubia red elements, the humanistic street photography control area features the leather texture of a professional camera, and the camera family supports a brand-new custom interface, making it look good and take better photos.
The world's first batch of Snapdragon 8 Gen2 leading editions set a new performance benchmark.As one of the world's first flagship phones equipped with the Snapdragon 8 Gen2 leading edition processor, the Nubia Z50S Pro chip upgrades the clock speed of the Cortex-X3 ultra-large core to 3.36GHz and the GPU clock speed to 719MHz.12 It features a unique Lingxi performance engine that can adaptively adjust the CPU, GPU, and a range of hardware units, achieving optimal performance matching through a deeply refined scheduling mechanism. To facilitate performance release, the new phone is equipped with a 4233mm2 ultra-large area biomimetic design VC, as well as multiple layers of heat dissipation materials such as diamond thermal gel, nano-carbon fiber, and graphene, with a total heat dissipation area of up to 42,833mm2. The back of the device is also equipped with nine high-precision NTC temperature sensors, which can sensitively detect subtle temperature changes and adjust the heat dissipation strategy in real time. In terms of gaming experience, the new device is equipped with the Lingxi Game Hub, which meticulously manages computing power and rendering requirements during the game process, mobilizes computing resources as needed, and features an e-sports-grade game frame stabilization engine that effectively improves game frame rate stability, reduces lag caused by fluctuations and frame drops, and results in a smoother picture. The esports-grade game space not only provides a variety of support tools and plugin libraries, but also a variety of fun features, making the gaming experience even cooler. 1.5K Super Retina-grade eye-protecting flat screen display with balanced power consumptionIn terms of screen, the Nubia Z50S Pro features a 6.78-inch AMOLED eye-protecting flat screen with a top-tier blue diamond arrangement, which can achieve an ultra-high resolution of 2800×1260 and a super-retina-level high pixel density of 452PPI; It features a cinema-level brilliant color display with 100% coverage of the DCI-P3 color gamut, 10-bit color depth, 1.07 billion color ranges, and a contrast ratio of 8000000:1; Supports 120Hz refresh rate and 1000Hz instantaneous touch sampling rate.
While boasting excellent display performance, the Nubia Z50S Pro screen also achieves balanced power consumption, featuring Q9 luminescent material, which reduces power consumption by 15% compared to the previous generation of luminescent materials. The tempered glass on the screen uses a deep multi-reinforcement process to provide hard-core drop resistance. The back case features an Italian "Carrara White" natural marble texture design, and uses 3D laser photolithography and nano-level coating to restore the natural crystal texture of the raw stone. The rear camera module features a rainbow holographic texture transparent ring design, which can bloom with unique and vibrant colors under different lighting angles, expressing Nubia's ultimate pursuit of light and shadow art.
The light and clean MyOS13 system helps users use it smoothly.The Nubia Z50S Pro is equipped with the MyOS13 system, which is light, clean, fun, and easy to use.
Lightweight firmware, most pre-installed applications can be uninstalled, few ads, and the system ad switch is turned off by default. The system has also upgraded the highly praised charging separation function in the game space to global system support, supporting only power supply without charging in more scenarios, maintaining a low-temperature feel while charging and playing, and bringing good body temperature and performance supply.
Price and purchase methodThe Nubia Z50S Pro will officially go on sale on July 27 on ZTE Mall, JD.com, Tmall, Douyin, JD.com Home, JD.com Computers & Digital, JD.com Appliances Super Experience Store, and other platforms.
The new 12GB+256GB version is priced at 3699 yuan; Four 1TB memory versions have been launched: the standard 12GB+1TB version is priced at 3999 yuan, and the 16GB+1TB version is priced at 4399 yuan; The Mirror of Light Special Edition 12GB+1TB is priced at 4099 yuan, and the 16GB+1TB version is priced at 4499 yuan.

entry.title: Xiaomi MIX Fold 3 | Aden's Space
entry.content: Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. Xiaomi MIX Fold 3: A perfect blend of thin and light folding and a true flagshipOn the evening of August 14, Xiaomi held the "2023 Lei Jun Annual Speech" event and officially launched the Xiaomi MIX Fold 3 foldable phone. This is a new upgrade for Xiaomi following the launch of its first foldable phone, the Xiaomi MIX Fold, last year, and it is also another innovative breakthrough for Xiaomi in the field of foldable screens. The Xiaomi MIX Fold 3 not only inherits the excellent design and performance of its predecessor, but also features comprehensive improvements in screen, hinge, imaging, and battery, creating a perfect blend of a thin and light foldable phone and a true flagship. Lightweight and thin body, super heat dissipationThe Xiaomi MIX Fold 3 features an 8.03-inch 2K+ ultra-high-definition internal screen and a 6.56-inch external screen, both made of the new E6 OLED light-emitting material. It boasts a global brightness of 1300 nits and a peak brightness of 2600 nits, supports a 1-120Hz LTPO adaptive refresh rate, and has also passed Dolby Vision and HDR 10+ certifications, delivering a visual experience with ultra-high clarity and color reproduction. The inner and outer screens are also equipped with dual front and rear light sensors and a 20-megapixel front-facing camera, making selfies clearer. The Xiaomi MIX Fold 3 has a very exquisite and thin body design, with a single-sided thickness of only 5.26mm, a folding thickness of 10.96mm (10.86mm for the Dragon Scale Fiber version), and a weight of 259g (255g for the Dragon Scale Fiber version). The phone features a high-precision brushed metal frame and a four-curved glass back cover. It is available in two color options: Moon Shadow Black and Star Gold, as well as a unique Dragon Scale Fiber Edition (black), showcasing a high-end and fashionable temperament. The Xiaomi MIX Fold 3 also boasts exceptional heat dissipation capabilities, featuring a 1850mm² ultra-thin stainless steel VC heat sink and high-density graphite, with a total heat dissipation area of 10,943mm², effectively reducing body temperature and power consumption. Meanwhile, the device also adopts a symmetrical 5G four-antenna layout and 5G super antenna technology, which greatly improves communication performance. Keel rotating shaft, free opening and closingOne of the biggest highlights of the Xiaomi MIX Fold 3 is its adoption of Xiaomi's self-developed keel hinge technology, which is a groundbreaking hinge design and a major technological breakthrough. It features an innovative three-stage connecting rod structure with 14 movable joints, 198 rotating shaft parts, and a 1800MPa super steel support structure, bringing unprecedented screen protection. Thanks to Xiaomi's keel hinge technology, the Xiaomi MIX Fold 3 has passed the TÜV Rheinland 500,000-fold certification, greatly extending its folding lifespan. The Xiaomi Keel hinge also brings an unprecedented folding experience. It uses an ultra-flat hinge float and UTG ultra-thin flexible glass to effectively smooth out screen creases and improve the screen's wear resistance and drop resistance. At the same time, it also supports free hovering at a wide angle of 45°-135°, which can be opened and closed at will according to different user needs and scenarios. When closed, the Xiaomi MIX Fold 3 offers an experience comparable to an iPhone, while when unfolded, it reveals the best foldable screen. Leica imaging, four full-focal length camerasThe Xiaomi MIX Fold 3 is currently the most powerful foldable flagship in terms of imaging capabilities. It is equipped with a Leica full-focal length quad-camera system, including a 50-megapixel main camera (Sony IMX800, 1/1.56 inch, memory alloy OIS, 1G+6P), a 12-megapixel ultra-wide-angle camera (OV13B10, 120°), a 10-megapixel portrait telephoto lens (Samsung S5K3K1, OIS), and a 10-megapixel periscope telephoto lens (Samsung S5K3K1, OIS). This imaging system not only passes Leica Summicron certification, but also adopts the new generation of Leica Color Science, Leica Classic and Leica Vivid dual image quality styles, as well as four Leica filters, supporting custom photography styles. The Xiaomi MIX Fold 3's imaging system boasts powerful photography capabilities, enabling 3.2X, 5X dual telephoto zoom, 10X hybrid zoom, and 30X digital zoom to capture clearer distant landscapes. It also supports functions such as 4K HDR10+ video recording, 8K video recording, video beautification, and video background blur, allowing users to shoot professional-grade video works anytime, anywhere. The Xiaomi MIX Fold 3 also supports AI video editing, which can intelligently identify highlights in videos and automatically add music and special effects to generate beautiful short videos. Surging battery, ultra-long battery lifeThe Xiaomi MIX Fold 3 uses two Xiaomi Surge batteries with a total capacity of 4800mAh, and is equipped with two Surge G1 power management chips and one Surge P2 fast charging chip, which together create powerful battery life. The device supports 67W wired fast charging and 50W wireless fast charging technology, which can fully charge the inner and outer screens in 40 minutes, and the battery life of both the inner and outer screens reaches 1.34 days. Whether watching videos, playing games, working and studying, or taking photos and videos, the Xiaomi MIX Fold 3 allows users to use it worry-free. sum upThe Xiaomi MIX Fold 3 is a perfect blend of a thin and light foldable phone and a true flagship phone. It not only boasts highlights such as a thin and light body, super heat dissipation, keel hinge, Leica imaging, and a surge battery, but also features flagship configurations such as a second-generation Snapdragon 8 leading edition processor, dual 1115 speakers, three microphones, and an X-axis linear motor. It also comes pre-installed with the MIUI Fold system adapted to large screens. This is a revolutionary foldable phone, ushering in a new era of foldable screens. The Xiaomi MIX Fold 3 began pre-sales on the evening of August 14th and officially went on sale on August 16th. It is priced at 8999 yuan (12GB + 256GB), 9999 yuan (12GB + 512GB), and 10999 yuan (16GB + 1TB), while the Dragon Scale Fiber Edition is priced at 11999 yuan (16GB + 1TB). If you're interested in this phone, you might want to give it a try and experience the perfect blend of slim and foldable design and a true flagship.

entry.title: Xiaomi 13 Ultra Half-Year Usage Report - Xiaomi 13 Ultra Demystification | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. This article is a six-month usage report of Xiaomi's 2023 imaging flagship. It is an original work by Aden and may not be reproduced without permission.
In early 2024, when the Xiaomi 14 Ultra was released, I bought a reduced-price Xiaomi annual imaging flagship at an extremely low price. This phone was once rated as having the strongest imaging capabilities in 2023, and it is also Xiaomi's second Ultra camera after its collaboration with Leica.
This picture clearly shows the exaggerated image quality of this phone. Some people say that this phone is not a qualified phone, but more like a camera. I. AppearanceThe most impressive aspect of this phone's appearance is undoubtedly its fastback design. My impression after using this phone is that "it succeeds and fails." Why do I say that? Because without this sloping back, this phone probably wouldn't be able to fit four large-sensor optical lenses. The reason it's a sloping back is because this sloping back gives the phone a very poor grip. I usually use this phone with my index finger pressed against the lens, otherwise the phone would flip over due to headaches. Besides the fastback, what makes this 13 Ultra different from ordinary phones is that its back panel adopts a padded design, which means that vegetable leather is filled in the middle frame, which is a unique design language. This design was carried over to the 14Ultra. One advantage of this design approach is that the middle frame can be made very solid. During my daily bare-bones use, I could clearly feel that the mid-frame was integrated with the entire phone, giving it a very rugged feel. II. Image SectionAs a flagship imaging device, the focus of this phone should be on imaging. First, let's talk about the mainThe main camera is an IMX989 from Sony. This CMOS chip originally appeared on the Xiaomi 12 Sultra and was jointly developed by Xiaomi and Sony. Xiaomi monopolized the market for six months before Sony allowed other mobile phone manufacturers to use it. This CMOS chip is 1 inch in size, and theoretically it can perform very well in low-light environments. But in actual use, I can only say that a perfectly good 1-inch screen was ruined by Xiaomi's terrible night view algorithm. In areas with many light signs, 13Ultra won't apply highlighter; the light signs will directly expose you to white. Then, when encountering warm or white light, there's a chance the white balance will drift, resulting in photos that are stark white with a hint of gray. It cannot handle complex light sources and has severe glare. I used the default mode when taking this picture; I didn't apply a lens film, and the lens was wiped clean. It is said that the Xiaomi 14 Ultra has improved coating, which should have a better effect than the 13 Ultra. The 13Ultra's night scene algorithm scheduling is very passive. The default mode is straight out with virtually no algorithm intervention. Only when the night scene mode is on can you clearly feel the traces of HDR algorithm processing (although it doesn't spin around). I think Xiaomi's strategy is very bad. Blindly pursuing film production speed will only lead to making a lot of bad films. Very severe red overflow During use, I also discovered another problem: Xiaomi (which could also be a problem with Leica toning) has a noticeable overflow when shooting red, and the trigger rate is 100%, which is not an accident. This may be due to algorithm bias, as red was not specifically optimized. Having discussed the disadvantages, are there any advantages? The answer is definitely there. Since collaborating with Leica, Xiaomi has been praising its shades. Actually, I think Xiaomi's tone control is quite successful. Leica Classic, Leica Vibrant, and Leica Monochrome HC are sufficient to handle various scenes. Since I started using this phone, my friends have all called me a "landscape photography master". Leica monochrome HC filter, shooting location: Hechai 1972 And the main camera uses a variable aperture. Although there are only two settings, F/1.9 and F/4, F/4 is enough to prevent me from having blurry edges when shooting text. However, there is very little "variable aperture" involved in the photography process; most scenes are shot at F/1.9 (ps: This variable aperture alone makes many beginners mistakenly think the lens is cracked). Then there is the medium coke.There's not much to say about the medium focal length lens; it's the best 3x lens I've ever used, and the 75mm gold focal length takes great photos. However, it should be noted that the 3.2x lens of the Xiaomi 13 Ultra is actually cropped to 68mm (2.6x). If you want to use the entire lens, you need to manually pull it back to 68mm. The only drawback is that it doesn't provide a floating lens module (macro). I don't quite understand why the 13Pro is equipped with a telephoto macro lens, but the Ultra lens is simplified. Finally, the telephoto lensThe telephoto lens is a 5x 858 lens, with viewing parameters of 1/2.51 inches and an aperture of F3.0. In actual testing, the telephoto capability is actually similar to, or even inferior to, the IMX586 on the Xiaomi 10 Supreme Commemorative Edition, Xiaomi 11 Ultra, and Xiaomi 12 Sultra. After searching online, I discovered that the IMX858 is 2x2OCL, which is not naturally suitable for long-distance viewing, and its quality is definitely not as good as the IMX586. However, during use, I found that its color accuracy was better than that of its predecessor (12SUltra), which can be considered an improvement. In the May update, Xiaomi provided the 13Ultra with the same AI super telephoto lens as the 14Ultra via OTA, which is essentially using a large AI model to draw more details. In actual use, the telephoto ability has indeed been improved, but the effect is still not as good as the 14Ultra. My opinion is that it's good enough to have it, and it's already good enough that you can't remember to give it to me. Haven't you heard that outdated flagships and dogs are not allowed inside? portraitPortraits are arguably one of the worst parts of your life. What I want to say is that the rear camera is bad, not the front camera. Xiaomi's front-facing portrait algorithm is currently in the first tier and has gained recognition from many women around me. Previously, rear-facing portraits were always Leica-toned, focusing on making people look sallow, and the edge blurring was also poorly handled. At the end of May, with the update of the AI super telephoto lens, the latest Master Portrait was also released to the Xiaomi 13 Ultra. However, after comparison, I found that it was probably only a filter released to the 13 Ultra. The photography page still has a terrible lens package design (the default 75mm cannot switch lenses, and switching lenses requires using the soft focus, rotating focus, Portrait and other terrible effects in the lens package), so it can be said that there has been no improvement. The main camera interface doesn't have a switch button for the fast EV (it's really incredible that the Turbo3 gives you rice but doesn't upzoom), the professional mode isn't preset, and the continuous zoom for video recording is still being held back. In summary, it boils down to one sentence: outdated flagships are not as good as dogs. Besides, the 13Ultra isn't outdated at all. The official price was adjusted to 1400 on July 11th, and now you can buy the 12+256 for 3999. If you treat old machines like this, who will buy them in the future? Therefore, compared to the 14 Ultra, Turbo3, and Civi4 Pro, the Xiaomi 13 Ultra currently lacks professional mode shade preset, continuous video zoom, EV quick adjustment, and a new portrait UI (focal length adjustment). In fact, these are all software-level things. If there are strong developers, they can even port them over, but Mi just won't release them. This does not include things like 4K120, which may be hardware-related. As a developer user, spending most of my time on couplets for three consecutive months is really unbearable. III. Surrounding ConfigurationThere's not much to say about the peripheral configurations of Xiaomi's devices; they basically have everything you need, and none of them are too bad. For example, charging is 90W wired and 50W wireless, and a 5000mAh battery is basically standard (just to complain, why does your Mi 5000's battery have such poor battery life? It only lasts 4-5 hours on 4G). Infrared remote control, IP68, dual speakers, and USB 3.2 will also be included. Speaking of the screen, I personally think the quality of this C7 screen from CSOT is quite good, and the eye protection is quite good, but the power consumption is a bit high. I feel like I've never reached the advertised peak speed of 2600 nits; I still can't see the screen clearly outdoors.Just take a look at the advertisements for your rice. One downside of this phone is that it gets very hot easily, and the brightness drops when it gets hot. The abnormal body temperature is also not easy to dissipate, and it all accumulates on the index finger supporting the phone under the lens, which is not a good experience on hot days. Whether it's 4G/5G or WiFi signals, I think they can be considered top-tier, comparable to Huawei's. The Wi-Fi is quite fast, but downloads are frequently congested, causing my Huawei's internet speed to be very poor. systemXiaomi released its self-developed system, Xiaomi HyperOS, also known as Surge OS, along with the Xiaomi 14 last November. Before MIUI 12, many people said that Xiaomi's system had many bugs. I didn't believe it at the time and after getting Xiaomi, I found it to be really good. Xiaomi's operating system is currently the most convenient for me to use. Its small functions and UI design are very user-friendly and efficient. Speaking of bugs, I didn't encounter many. Maybe I'm not very sensitive to lag, but it was okay, except for the occasional slight frame drop. Adding your favorite features to MIUI and Surge after rooting will make it easier to use. Before I sold my Xiaomi 13 Ultra, it was the development version 1.0.24.7.8.DEV. Overall, compared to the first version, all the bugs have been fixed, the overall scheduling and overheating have also decreased a lot, and the system is generally smoother (of course, there is still a gap compared to the current T0). Never give up on a good phone just because you hear the system is bad. Everyone was hyping vivo's OriginOS 4, but after my recommendation, a friend bought the X100 Pro, and after experiencing it, I felt it was just so-so.Whether the system is good or not, you have to use it yourself to know.。 sum upOverall, the Xiaomi 13 Ultra is not a decent phone. Its distorted design, poor heat dissipation, and overheating provide a user experience that is inferior to its own Xiaomi 13, or even performance phones like the K60 and K70. However, his photography is indeed remarkable. Before the Xiaomi 14 Ultra came out, it was indeed the most well-rounded camera overall. There's a saying that goes: there's no such thing as an unsuitable machine, only an unsuitable price. Now the price of a used 13 Ultra has dropped below 3000, and you can buy a brand new 12+256 for 3999. If you have a limited budget but want to buy a phone with decent photography, the 13Ultra is definitely your best choice.

entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-08-24: AI Race Heats Up, Geopolitical Risks Affect Markets | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeOver the past 24 hours, the common keyword in the market remained "uncertainty pricing": geopolitical situations continued to affect energy transportation and risk appetite, while tech giants competed for AI infrastructure with larger-scale financing and capital expenditures. China's domestic consumption promotion policies are moving from the document stage to the banking implementation stage. For Australian dollar holders, the RMB against the Australian dollar is temporarily maintained in the conversion range of approximately 4.84. Travel, study abroad, or cross-border payments can continue to be exchanged in batches to reduce the impact of fluctuations at a single point in time.
Five key news items1. The United States is considering additional sanctions against Iran, and energy transportation risks remain a market variable.The United States is expected to announce a new round of sanctions against Iran, but Iran has stated that the measures will not be effective. Concerns about shipping disruptions near the Strait of Hormuz remain, meaning that crude oil and transportation costs may continue to command a risk premium. The most noteworthy issues to watch in the short term are the targets of sanctions, the speed of shipping recovery, and whether rising oil prices will be further transmitted to inflation expectations and interest rate pricing.Source:Reuters 2. Alibaba plans to place HK$80 billion in new shares, with all funds invested in AI.Alibaba announced plans to issue new shares for a total consideration of approximately HK$80 billion, and plans to invest all the net proceeds in full-stack AI capabilities, including computing infrastructure. This scale shows that leading platforms still have a long-term assessment of the AI competition cycle: in the short term, capital expenditures and equity dilution pressures will increase, but they may also strengthen the synergy between cloud computing, models and applications.Source:Alibaba Group Official Announcement 3. Nvidia will release its financial report on August 26, and the market awaits verification of AI demand.Nvidia has confirmed that it will release its results for the second quarter of fiscal year 2027 on August 26, US time. As major tech companies continue to increase their investment in AI, this financial report will serve as an important window into computing power demand, chip supply, and whether data center capital expenditures can continue. The key here is not only revenue growth, but also management's statements on subsequent orders, product iterations, and supply capacity.Source:NVIDIA Investor Relations 4. China's consumer loan interest subsidies are expanding, and the policy is beginning to be implemented by banks.Several large banks have successively updated their arrangements for implementing interest subsidies for personal consumer loans. Related reports show that the annual interest subsidy limit has been increased from 3,000 yuan to 5,000 yuan, and the coverage has been further extended to scenarios such as automobiles, home decoration, and consumer installment plans. Whether the policy can effectively stimulate demand depends on the convenience of bank processing, the decline in actual financing costs for residents, and data on automobile and durable goods consumption.Source:China Economic Net；Policy Background of China Government Website 5. Syria and Israel held US-mediated talks in an attempt to establish a de-escalation mechanism.Syrian and Israeli representatives held talks in Jordan, mediated by the United States, focusing on practical mechanisms for reducing military operations, arrests, and reciprocal incidents, and attempting to restore security arrangements. The talks themselves do not equate to the disappearance of differences, but if an enforceable liaison and constraint mechanism can be established subsequently, it may reduce the probability of regional conflicts continuing to spill over.Source:Reuters (Yahoo News (Reprinted)；Al Jazeera RMB to Australian Dollar Exchange Rate CardThe Bank of China's foreign exchange quote is 2026-08-24 18:00:14 Display:

Bank prices will be updated daily, and the actual transaction price will vary depending on the bank, channel, and transaction time.Source:Bank of China Foreign Exchange Rates Market Correlation and Today's ObservationToday's information can be connected into a clear main thread: geopolitical risks may raise energy and logistics costs, AI investment continues to push funds towards computing infrastructure, and consumption-boosting policies attempt to support domestic demand. For ordinary readers, there are three things to focus on: whether crude oil prices will experience a new round of fluctuations due to details of sanctions; Can Nvidia's financial report prove that AI capital expenditures can still be realized? Has the experience of applying for consumer interest subsidies at banks truly improved? Regarding exchange rates, if there is a clear Australian dollar spending plan in the future, it is still a safer approach to exchange currencies in batches based on time or target price, rather than betting on the direction of a single day. entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-08-25: Reserve Bank of Australia turns hawkish, global policy constraints tighten | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeOver the past 24 hours, market attention has focused on both policy constraints and technical expertise: while the Reserve Bank of Australia kept interest rates unchanged, the meeting minutes continued to retain the possibility of a rate hike; The United States simultaneously tightened economic restrictions on Iran and some immigrant visa policies. At the same time, China and India resumed high-level border talks, and a new self-developed artificial intelligence model emerged in the professional services industry. These changes collectively send a signal that the global policy environment remains cautious, uncertainties in energy, interest rates, and cross-border flows have not completely subsided, and competition in artificial intelligence is gradually extending from general models to specialized fields such as law, taxation, and compliance.
Five key news items1. The Reserve Bank of Australia reserves the possibility of further rate hikes.The Reserve Bank of Australia released the minutes of its August monetary policy meeting. The committee had previously unanimously decided to maintain the cash rate target at 4.35%, but the meeting also discussed the reasons for raising rates by 25 basis points. Some committee members believe that the risk of rising inflation may still materialize, and they do not rule out further tightening of policies if necessary. The minutes expect inflation to gradually return to near the midpoint of the target range by the end of 2027. For families, this means that mortgage and consumer credit costs are unlikely to decrease significantly in the short term; For the Australian dollar, maintaining high interest rates for an extended period usually provides some support, but energy price and employment data will still influence subsequent judgments. Source:Minutes of the Reserve Bank of Australia's August monetary policy meeting 2. The United States expands sanctions against Iran.The United States announced expanded sanctions against Iran, with a new list covering 60 individuals, entities, and vessels, and warned that third parties that continue to conduct some business with Iran may lose their eligibility to enter the dollar financial system. However, this round of measures does not include Chinese financial institutions suspected of involvement in Iranian oil trade. This round of policies will continue to affect Middle East shipping, oil supply, and international settlement risks. The current measures have not yet adopted the most severe option, but if sanctions are expanded to more financial institutions or trading partners, compliance and transportation costs for businesses could rise further. Source:Reuters: US expands sanctions against Iran 3. The United States plans to revoke nonimmigrant visas for some asylum seekers.The U.S. State Department said it is coordinating with the Department of Homeland Security to identify and revoke some nonimmigrant visas held by individuals who entered the country on a short-term business or tourist visa and subsequently applied for asylum. The official number of people involved has not yet been released; Reuters, citing the Associated Press, estimated that the potential number could reach 200,000. Visa revocation does not necessarily mean immediate deportation, but the individual may lose their original business or tourist status. If fully implemented, this policy will further increase policy uncertainty in travel, study, and long-term residency planning in the United States. Source:Reuters: The United States plans to revoke visas for some asylum seekers. 4. China and India will hold their 25th meeting of special representatives on the border issue in Beijing.The Chinese Foreign Ministry announced that Wang Yi will hold the 25th meeting of special representatives on the China-India border issue with Indian National Security Advisor Doval in Beijing on August 25. This mechanism is an important high-level channel for the two countries to resolve border disputes and maintain border stability. The information released so far only confirms the meeting arrangements; there is no outcome document yet. If both sides can make progress on border management and communication mechanisms, it will help reduce the risk of friction and create a more stable environment for economic, trade and people-to-people exchanges. Source:Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs: Arrangements for the Meeting of Special Representatives on the China-India Border Question 5. Thomson Reuters launches its own professional large language model.Thomson Reuters releases its first autonomously controlled large language model, "Thomson". The company stated that the model starts with an open foundation model and is trained with professional content from Westlaw, Practical Law, Checkpoint, and Reuters, with a total investment of approximately US$40 million. It will initially be used for CoCounsel Legal's document analysis function. This indicates that enterprise AI competition is shifting from simply pursuing larger general-purpose models to vertical models with industry data, professional verification processes, and lower inference costs. The relevant performance data currently mainly comes from the company's own evaluation, and more independent testing is still needed. Source:Thomson Reuters Official release RMB to Australian Dollar Exchange Rate CardThe Bank of China's spot selling price for Australian dollars announced at 10:10:22 (Beijing time) on August 25, 2026, was as follows:

AI investment continues to support corporate expansion and is rapidly entering professional services such as law; China, on the other hand, uses investment promotion platforms to strengthen policy communication and foreign investment services. For the market, growth has not yet slowed down, but interest rate and energy risks are still enough to amplify asset price volatility.

IMF: Global economy withstands energy shocks, but fiscal risks riseInternational Monetary Fund Managing Director Georgieva said the global economy has been more resilient than expected to the energy shocks caused by the Iran war and the disruption of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.
