Therefore, the market still needs to observe whether industrial investment can form a broader cycle of income and demand. The core variables in the coming days are whether oil prices can fall back below $100 and stabilize, whether global long-term bond yields will continue to rise, whether shipping in the Red Sea will deteriorate, and whether AI security disclosure will be rapidly upgraded from a voluntary action by enterprises to a regulatory standard. If energy risks ease, risky assets may get a breather; If oil prices and bond yields rise again in tandem, global markets will continue to trade a more typical stagflationary risk premium.
Cover image:Eduard Pretsi / Unsplash

entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-09-19: Energy Shocks and AI Security Reshaping Risk Pricing | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeOver the past 24 hours, global markets have refocused their pricing around "energy shocks - inflation - interest rates - risk appetite": Middle Eastern shipping and energy transportation remain in high-risk areas, European fuel and natural gas prices have risen, and policy levels have begun to discuss imposing a windfall profits tax on energy companies. The Bank of Japan raised its policy interest rate to 1.25%, further squeezing the low-cost yen financing space for global funds; With loan interest rates expected to remain unchanged for the 16th consecutive month, China continues to rely on industrial upgrading and structural policies to support domestic demand. In the AI sector, OpenAI encountered an "ethical attack" test conducted within a vulnerability bounty framework, demonstrating that AI tools are lowering the threshold for complex cyberattacks. The common theme is that supply-side shocks are raising nominal growth and policy uncertainty, while technology security incidents have brought the regulatory discount of overvalued assets back to the forefront.
Five key news items1. The Bank of Japan raised interest rates to 1.25%, and yen financing transactions face repricing.The Bank of Japan raised its benchmark interest rate to 1.25%, the highest level in about 30 years, while policymakers simultaneously released the possibility of further rate hikes. Drivers include rising energy prices, a weaker yen, and continued domestic inflationary pressures. Japanese institutional investors hold large amounts of overseas bond and equity assets. Rising interest rates may not immediately trigger a large-scale capital outflow, but they will increase the funding costs for carry trades and compress marginal demand for U.S. Treasury bonds, global credit bonds, and overvalued technology stocks. For the market, the key is not just domestic interest rates in Japan, but whether the yen will continue to appreciate, whether domestic wages and core inflation will continue to rise, and whether Japanese investors will begin to increase their allocation to domestic bonds. If capital outflows accelerate, global long-term yields and US dollar financing conditions may tighten simultaneously; If the yen remains weak, it indicates that energy shocks and interest rate differentials still dominate.Source: WSJ 2. Soaring fuel and natural gas prices in Europe spark discussions about a unified windfall profits tax in the EU.Fuel prices in many European countries have risen above €2.70 per liter, and benchmark natural gas prices have increased by about 150% compared to a year ago. The energy crisis is beginning to shift from a market issue to a fiscal and political one. The German Finance Minister called on the EU to study imposing a windfall profits tax on energy companies, while France, Italy, and Spain each took subsidies, tax cuts, or targeted support measures to buffer pressure on residents and the transportation industry. The direct background to the price increase is the disruption of shipping and supply chains by the Middle East conflict, while the indirect impact is the resurgence of inflation expectations and the simultaneous pressure on corporate costs and residents' real incomes. Going forward, it remains to be seen whether the EU will form a unified tax system, whether subsidies will widen the fiscal deficit, and whether energy prices will be transmitted to core inflation through industrial and service prices. If policy shifts towards large-scale subsidies, European bond supply and sovereign yield spreads could once again become the focus of the market.Source: The Guardian 3. China's LPR is expected to remain unchanged for the 16th consecutive month in September, indicating a more structurally loose approach.A Reuters poll shows that China's one-year and five-year loan market prime rates are expected to remain unchanged at 3.00% and 3.50% respectively in September, marking the 16th consecutive month. The backdrop is that major central banks around the world are shifting towards tightening, while China's credit demand remains dragged down by weak real estate and local government financing. The People's Bank of China prefers to support key sectors through targeted instruments, relending, and industrial policies rather than significantly lowering benchmark interest rates. The impact on the economy lies in the fact that stable nominal financing costs help avoid exchange rate and bank interest rate spread pressures, but it also means that real estate, household leverage, and local investment will not recover quickly from a single interest rate cut. The pace of credit, social financing, real estate sales, and fiscal policy in September needs to be observed. If domestic demand remains weak, the policy focus may shift to consumption support, equipment upgrades, and investment in advanced manufacturing and technology, rather than a comprehensive interest rate cut.Source: Reuters 4. AI-assisted "ethical attacks" expose the boundaries of corporate account and code permissions.Under the vulnerability bounty framework, the cybersecurity research team, using Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol, completed an "ethical attack" test on OpenAI systems: the researchers first obtained accounts through employee forums, and then used GitHub permissions to initiate harmless code modification requests, ultimately proving that AI tools can significantly lower the professional threshold required for complex intrusions. OpenAI stated that it has fixed the vulnerability, and the researchers received a $6,500 reward. The focus of the incident is not the large-scale theft of sensitive code, but rather that AI is making the "discovery entry point - orchestration tool - completion operation" link faster and cheaper. The impact on the industry is that companies must re-examine the scope of tool calls for authentication, least privileges, code repository isolation, and AI agents. The impact on valuation is that security expenditures and regulatory costs may become new fixed costs for model companies. It remains to be seen whether more real attacks driven by AI agents will emerge, and whether regulators will require model manufacturers to disclose the boundaries of their high-risk capabilities.Source: The Guardian 5. Bolivia received a $1.9 billion IMF agreement in exchange for foreign exchange and fiscal stability.The Bolivian Congress has approved an expanded fund arrangement with the International Monetary Fund of approximately $1.9 billion, with the aim of alleviating foreign exchange shortages, fiscal deterioration, and insufficient international reserves, and seeking to leverage more than $5 billion in additional funding from institutions such as the World Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank. The government disclosed net international reserves of approximately US$3.17 billion, but only US$52 million in available liquid assets; The agreement calls for reducing the fiscal deficit, improving monetary discipline, implementing a more flexible exchange rate mechanism, and phasing out fuel subsidies, while providing protection for vulnerable groups. This event is representative: in an environment of high global financing costs and rising energy and dollar risks, resource-based emerging markets still need to exchange fiscal consolidation and price reforms for external liquidity. Subsequent variables to be observed include the implementation of exchange rate reforms, the social backlash against the withdrawal of fuel subsidies, whether reserves will rebound, and whether IMF funds can truly drive a recovery in private investment and imports.Source: Reuters Market Correlation and Today's ObservationIn terms of interest rates, the simultaneous existence of Japan's interest rate hikes and European energy inflation has presented the global yield curve with a combination of "hawkish policies + damaged growth". At the exchange rate level, whether the yen continues to strengthen will affect carry trading and demand for dollar assets; The euro depends on energy import bills, fiscal subsidies, and the European Central Bank's tolerance for secondary inflation. At the commodity level, crude oil and natural gas remain core variables in risk appetite. If transportation bottlenecks continue, energy prices will continue to be transmitted to industrial products, aviation, chemicals, and consumer spending. Regarding technology valuations, the AI security incident serves as a reminder to the market: the closer the model's capabilities are to the executable agent, the more security investment, compliance costs, and liability boundaries will be included in profit forecasts. Valuations based solely on computing power and user growth need to be discounted. In China, the unchanged LPR means that policies place greater emphasis on structural support, and the market should focus on observing the combined data of consumption, real estate, local government bonds and advanced manufacturing, rather than focusing on just one interest rate cut. The most important observation windows today are whether there will be a substantial easing in energy transportation, whether the yen and US Treasury yields will fluctuate in the same direction, and whether AI companies will begin to translate security incidents into stricter product permissions and disclosure systems. Cover image :You Le / Unsplash (Original image page）

entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-09-20: Saudi Arabia Attack and US-China Talks Impact Energy and Technology Expectations | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeNew developments on September 19 brought two types of risks to the market simultaneously: on the one hand, the Houthi rebels in Yemen claimed to have attacked the Saudi capital, plumes of smoke appeared near Riyadh airport, and the vulnerability of energy transportation in the Red Sea and the Gulf was once again tested; On the other hand, Chinese and American finance officials have finalized a meeting in New York, with artificial intelligence security and trade issues on the agenda ahead of next week's high-level diplomacy. In China, the investigation into unfair competition in the platform economy has expanded, and members of the People's Bank of China's Monetary Policy Committee have warned that artificial intelligence may further amplify "strong supply and weak demand". Overseas AI companies are weighing new models, security commitments, and IPO expectations. The common theme is that supply capacity and security risks change rapidly, and whether demand, institutional arrangements, and policy coordination can keep up will determine how energy premiums, technology valuations, and China's domestic demand expectations are repriced. There was little trading over the weekend, and the full impact of the news on prices remains to be seen at the market opening in the new week. Previously, the market was already worried that rising energy prices and high financing costs would squeeze corporate profits. This new attack risk, regulatory actions, and diplomatic arrangements force investors to weigh immediate supply shocks against slower institutional changes. The title refers to expected changes, not price movements that have already occurred.
Five key news items1. Houthi rebels claim attack on Riyadh, putting alternative energy transport routes under renewed pressure.On September 19, the Houthi rebels in Yemen claimed to have attacked "sensitive locations" in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, with missiles and drones. Reuters reporters photographed black smoke and flames near the main airport. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted missiles heading toward Riyadh and thwarted attacks on several cities, including the Red Sea port of Yanbu. The extent of the damage to the airport facilities is still pending official verification. The Houthi rebels claimed this move was in response to an earlier attack on the Yemeni capital, Sana'a. The conflict stems from the fact that the Red Sea route has become an important alternative for Gulf energy exports when passage through the Strait of Hormuz is blocked, and the Houthi rebels have recently taken action against Saudi ships and energy facilities. If the Red Sea and onshore facilities face threats simultaneously, tanker insurance, freight rates, and crude oil risk premiums may rise, which could then be transmitted to fuel, inflation expectations, and the central bank's interest rate path. The focus going forward will be on actual facility damage, whether port shipments have been disrupted, the scale of shipping detours, and whether mediation can reduce the frequency of attacks. In particular, it is important to distinguish between attack claims, scene footage, and verified production losses: these three represent completely different supply impacts.Source: Reuters 2. Chinese and US finance officials plan to meet in New York; AI security is on the trade agenda.According to Reuters, citing sources familiar with the matter, arrangements finalized on September 19 indicate that U.S. Treasury Secretary Besant and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng are scheduled to meet in New York at 10:30 a.m. Eastern Time on Sunday to discuss artificial intelligence security, trade, and other economic issues. The meeting was held at JPMorgan Chase headquarters, which only provided the venue and did not participate in the agenda. The talks are scheduled ahead of US President Trump's hosting of Chinese President*at the White House next week. The market should distinguish between "confirmed meeting" and "reaching an agreement": the report did not publish the negotiation text, nor did it promise to adjust tariffs or technical restrictions. A new highlight is the explicit inclusion of artificial intelligence security in the financial dialogue, which may link computing power, model usage rules, and terms of trade. For businesses, policy predictability affects cross-border orders, investment, and supply chain arrangements; For exchange rates and risk assets, whether the wording tends to soften is more important than the location of the meeting. Pay attention to the announcements from both sides after the meeting, the specific working mechanisms, and whether the summit between the heads of state next week will yield actionable results. Simply announcing continued communication may improve market sentiment in the short term, but companies still need to wait for clear rules before changing their investment plans.Source: Reuters 3. China investigates multiple online booking platforms, extending competition policies to hotels and travel.Chinese state media reported on September 19 that Beijing's market supervision authorities have launched an investigation into Beijing Sankuai Information Technology Co., Ltd., a subsidiary of Meituan, for suspected violations of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. Alibaba's subsidiaries Hangzhou Taomei Aviation Services, Tongcheng Network Technology, and Tujia-related companies are also included in the investigation. The relevant companies expressed their cooperation, and the investigation does not equate to a conclusion of illegality. Previously, regulators had fined Ctrip 5.2 billion yuan for monopolistic practices in online hotel bookings; This involvement of multiple platforms demonstrates that regulators are focusing on industry-specific issues such as pricing, platform rules, and the business environment for merchants. Hotel and travel consumption is highly correlated with platform traffic. If the transaction rules are adjusted, it may increase the platform's compliance costs and change commission and promotion revenue in the short term. In the long term, it may affect hotels' bargaining power, consumer choices and service prices. Investors need to wait for the investigation's determination and rectification details; the penalty standards from previous cases cannot be directly applied to the new investigation. We will subsequently observe platform disclosures, changes in merchant fees, and the specific definitions of regulatory restrictions on cross-platform operations. The decline in consumer prices is not an inevitable result, and increased competition may also prompt platforms to cut subsidies. The actual effect must be verified by transaction data.Source: Reuters 4. Central Bank policy advisors warn that AI may exacerbate China's "strong supply and weak demand" situation.Huang Yiping, a member of the Monetary Policy Committee of the People's Bank of China, said at the Beijing Economic Forum on September 19 that the widespread application of artificial intelligence and the acceleration of innovation may further deepen and last longer the imbalance between strong supply and weak demand. He advocates increasing the proportion of residents' income in the economy through market-oriented reforms and considering increasing central government borrowing to help repair the balance sheets of local governments, financial institutions, and enterprises. This is a public recommendation from policy advisors and should not be considered as the central bank announcing new fiscal or monetary measures. The logic is that AI improves productivity and export supply, but it may not simultaneously increase residents' purchasing power; If domestic demand is insufficient, corporate profits, employment, prices, and debt repayment may all be under pressure. For the market, the focus is shifting from simple computing power investment to consumer revenue, local fiscal recovery, and corporate pricing power. Next, we need to look at official policy documents, residents' income and retail data, prices, and local government financing to determine whether demand-side support is keeping pace with supply expansion.Source: Reuters 5. Anthropic is considering the timing of its new model release, as AI competition and security commitments clash.An exclusive Reuters report published on September 19, citing three sources familiar with the matter, reported that Anthropic is considering launching a new model to compete with OpenAI following its release of GPT-6 Astra this month. The company has not commented on the report, and the specific release date has not yet been determined. The report, citing a sample from enterprise spending platform Ramp, stated that Astra accounts for approximately 13% of its enterprise AI spending, while Anthropic's Claude Fable accounts for approximately 8%. This reflects the spending composition of a specific platform and is not equivalent to the market share of the entire enterprise. Anthropic’s CEO had previously called for a slowdown in the release of new capabilities to address security concerns, while the company also had to weigh its IPO expectations, model evaluation, and revenue growth. High interest rates and competition with open-source models have increased investors' demands for cash flow, and the iteration speed of leading models will also affect customer procurement, computing power spending, and security costs. The next step will be to determine whether the model is officially released, independent performance and security evaluations, corporate contract renewals, and revenue quality, rather than judging the outcome solely based on release rumors. If the security review is delayed, customers may temporarily switch to competing products; If a hasty launch encounters major problems, subsequent compliance costs will also backfire on growth.Source: Reuters Market Correlation and Today's ObservationThe first thing to test when the market opens next week is whether the Saudi attack has caused actual supply or shipping disruptions: if there are only risk warnings, the oil price premium may fall. If delays or other key milestones are damaged, rising crude oil and freight rates will push up inflation expectations again and limit the room for major central banks to ease interest rates. Changes in interest rate expectations will affect the US dollar, Japanese yen, and emerging market currencies, while suppressing the valuation of long-term growth assets through discount rates. The US-China talks may change risk appetite for the RMB, Asian export chains, and semiconductor-related assets, but policy changes should be judged based on official announcements rather than anonymous information. The China platform survey, along with Huang Yiping's view, points to domestic demand: if competition rules reduce business costs, there will be a lack of residents' income and local fiscal recovery, and consumption improvement may still be limited. In terms of technology, the AI model competition not only drives demand for data centers and chips, but also increases security assessments and capital expenditures; Valuations need to be tested by real paid growth and profit margins. Observe oil and gas spot and shipping prices, US Treasury yields and US dollar trends, RMB expectations, platform company announcements, and verifiable operating indicators of AI companies to avoid confusing risks at different time scales. Weekend news tends to amplify expectations when liquidity is low, and prices, trading volume, and policy statements after the official opening are more likely to test whether the market has truly changed its judgment. Cover image:You Le / Unsplash

entry.title: Why Jev is so popular: When AI stops writing answers and makes judgments for software | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. TypeSafe AI Official Review Chart: Jev Compares to Other Models in Workflow Accuracy and Cost Image source:TypeSafe AI's Jev Release Article。 This is the company's own workflow evaluation diagram. See below for specific comparison conditions and limitations. An email arrived: "You've deducted money from my account twice. If it doesn't get processed today, I'll file a complaint." The customer service system's next task isn't mysterious: identify this as a billing issue, determine if it's urgent, find the order, and then decide who to hand it over to. In the past, we might have given an email to a chat model, asked it to write an analysis, or had it spit out a piece of JSON in a specified format. Now a company is asking another question:If software only needs a few judgments, why does it have to make the model write an answer first? This company is TypeSafe AI. Its Jev, launched on September 15, 2026, targets precisely these small judgments hidden in software processes. It receives a description of the situation and a pre-set question, and returns options, scores, or probabilities that the program can read directly. For example: Is this email a "bill" or "technical support"? Did the customer explicitly request a refund? How emotional were you? These answers are then handed over to ordinary programs for processing.Release notes for TypeSafeandProduct DocumentationBoth describe it as a decision-making model for software calls. This approach is worth looking at carefully, but it can easily be overstated. Jev is not a machine that automatically handles all complaints; It answers questions, and company procedures and employees are still responsible for verifying deductions, executing refunds, and handling exceptions. Let's put it into a real process first.Assume that the system has received customer emails, order records, and refund rules. Traditional chat models can also understand these materials. You can ask it to say, "Summarize the situation, give priorities, departments, and refund recommendations." It might write something that sounds like a human customer service executive, or it can return JSON as requested. The developer then reads the results into the program, checks whether the fields are complete and the values are valid, and then decides on the next step. Jev is used more like giving it several multiple-choice questions at once:
Questions asked to the model What might be returned? How to use the software
Which department should this email be sent to? Options such as billing, after-sales service, and technical support, and their respective weights. Forward to the corresponding queue
Does the customer request a refund? The probability of "yes" Decide whether to initiate a refund verification
How urgent is the customer? Scoring on a preset level Determine the order of processing
The answers in the table only illustrate the format.hypothetical exampleThis is not the result I get when I actually call Jev. When actually deploying, the criteria for judging the problem should be clearly written, and exits such as "other" or "unable to judge" should be allowed. Just because a customer says "money was deducted twice" doesn't mean that the financial system actually made two valid deductions; Checking transaction records cannot be replaced by tone of voice. Jev's strength lies in this interface. Developers first specify the range of answers that can be given, and the model makes judgments within that range. Subsequent programs can then be divided accordingly. It transforms information that was originally hidden in a long piece of text into values that can be used directly in the software process.Definition of three problems in official documentsYes: Choice selects one of the given options; Score scores at a given level; Noul answers a true or false question and gives the probability of "yes". The latter does not have a separate confidence Field. What exactly is the difference between it and ChatGPT?The strength of chat models is their flexibility. Ask it to explain a contract, write a reply, or modify a piece of code; the answer often has no fixed shape. It usually generates text gradually; Even if you end up with just one department name, you're still completing a text generation task. Jev predetermines the optional answers and question types, and processes multiple independent questions in parallel in a single request. It is not responsible for writing that email to reassure the client.
What do you need Chat-based AI is more convenient Jev is a more suitable scenario
Write a measured reply Can be drafted and modified directly Do not generate reply body
Choose a destination in a fixed department It can be done, usually requiring constraints and checking the output. You can return directly to the default options
Simultaneously judge more than a dozen independent small problems You can answer in the specified format. The design goal is to give these judgments in parallel.
Dealing with new questions without preset answers Flexible exploration and interpretation First, design the question and answer range.
This is to correct a common misconception: today's generative models already support structured output, tool calls, and formatting constraints, rather than just outputting a paragraph of prose. The difference between the two lies not in "the former absolutely cannot be left to the program, only the latter can," but in their main design goals, the way they generate answers, and the cost and speed trade-offs between multiple small judgments. Complex cases may not be suitable for breaking down all judgments into independent multiple-choice questions.TypeSafe documentationIt is recommended to break down questions that require multi-step analysis and then combine the answers with a program. What are people doing with Jev now?Jev has only been released for a short time, and the following are mainly open-source projects publicly available in the community. They are not official products of TypeSafe, and the demonstration results in the project README should not be taken as general conclusions for the production environment. However, they are well suited to explaining the location of the Jev: the Jev is responsible for making a clearly defined judgment, and the actual clicks, deletions, diversions, or orders are still done by other programs.
Jev Ultrafast: A browser proxy. It organizes the controls on the webpage into numbered action spaces, allowing the Jev to choose "which button to click, which option to select, whether to scroll," etc. Only when you really need to input free text do you hand it over to a small language model to generate text. The Google Flights example in the project also independently examines the final page, demonstrating that it is searching for Flights, not paying for and booking tickets for users. Jev Review: A phased code review tool. It first assesses the risk, then selects the file type, evidence, and possible problem mechanisms, then gives a severity score and decides whether it needs to be forwarded to a specific reviewer, and finally displays the report on the local page. It itself notes that the report is a review tip, not a conclusion that a defect has been proven. fast-jev-compaction: A context cleaning plug-in for Claude Code. Instead of letting another chat model regenerate the entire history, it lets Jev determine which tool calls and results are still worth keeping and which can be deleted or shortened; The original text that has been retained continues to be retained as is. This is a very intuitive example of Jev making "trade-offs" rather than writing answers. typesafe-computer-useA macOS computer operation experiment. The program reads the screen using OCR and the accessibility tree, and then lets Jev choose the next step from a limited number of actions; The writing model is called only when you want to enter a piece of free text. It demonstrates breaking down the "operating computer" into many cheap little options, but still requiring permissions, deterministic screen reading, and safe stop conditions. jev-trader: A trading experiment connecting the Kuru MON-USDC order book on Monad. For each block, it asks Jev whether to buy or sell, then places a corresponding price limit order and pushes the decision and transaction results to the dashboard. By default, the project can only run simulations; Even so, this experiment should not be considered a guarantee of returns or investment advice; it is more suitable for observing the role of JEVs in low-latency decision-making.
These projects show that Jev is currently most often placed "before action": browsers prepare clicks, code reviewers prepare reports, proxies prepare context compression, and trading programs prepare orders. It's not as simple as replacing one large model with another; rather, it reduces the steps that originally required generating long answers to a few small judgments that the program can repeatedly call. What can it do for non-software engineers?If you're not a developer, the most common misconception is that Jev seems to be just another AI tool that requires you to open a chat window and learn prompts. In fact, ordinary users are more likely to use it indirectly in software that already has Jev integrated, rather than talking directly to Jev.
Everyday scene What can Jev judge in the background? The final result you see
Numerous emails and customer service messages Is this a billing, after-sales, or technical issue? Is it urgent? Is a refund explicitly requested? Emails are automatically placed in the appropriate queue, and ambiguous or high-risk emails are handed over to manual labor.
Invoices, reimbursements and application materials Are the materials complete? Do you want to trigger a rule? Is additional proof required? First, screen out any missing materials or items that need to be reviewed to reduce manual review of each item.
The information and notifications are too mixed. Is this news important? Is it a reminder, bill, advertisement, or to-do list? Automatically categorize, remind, or silently process instead of pushing everything to you
Other AI agents are performing tasks. Should we continue next, which tool should we call, or should we stop and ask people? Fewer unnecessary model calls and fewer uncertain automated actions.
These things are not done by Jev alone. When it's actually implemented, someone still needs to design the problems, options, thresholds, and follow-up actions. The software is also responsible for reading real data, recording results, and handling exceptions. For non-developers, the value of Jev is not that it allows you to learn another API, but that it makes it faster and cheaper for the customer service, office, browser, or automation tools you are using to make a lot of repetitive judgments, and it is also easier to set the boundary of "leave it to someone else if you are unsure". Why probability is more useful than a definitive answerReturn to the duplicate deduction email. If the system only receives "yes" or "no" when determining whether a refund is explicitly requested, it is easy to take excessive actions when encountering vague wording. If you can see the weight the model assigns to "yes," the program can set rules: clearly proceed to subsequent verification; If the information is vague, please ask the customer for additional information; The key steps involving genuine refunds are still checked and executed within the company's authority. There are two easily confused numbers here. For right and wrong questions, Noul gives the probability of "yes". For multiple-choice and scoring questions, Jev provides a probability distribution for each option or level, and also offers a probability distribution calculated from the degree of distribution concentration. confidence。 **This confidence is not "the probability of this answer being correct". **If the weights of the three departments are 90%, 7%, and 3% respectively, it indicates that the model's judgments are very concentrated; As for whether the judgment of focusing on the "billing department" is correct, real cases are still needed to test it.Official explanation of confidenceIt also clearly distinguishes between it and probability, and suggests setting different thresholds based on business risks. There is also a word called "calibration". In layman's terms, if the model answers "yes" about 80% of a large number of verifiable similar questions, the proportion of those that actually answer "yes" should also be close to 80%. Such numbers make it easier to design the boundaries between automated processing and manual review. TypeSafe calls its training method RLCDThis means that reinforcement learning is performed on calibrated decisions. It hopes that in addition to providing answers, the model can also express uncertainty more honestly.Release NotesThis goal was explained; However, publicly available information is insufficient for the outside world to independently reconstruct the training details, nor can it be concluded that all scenarios are well-calibrated based solely on product introductions. Where do speed and cheapness come from?You only ask the security guard, "Can this person come in?" and he writes a one-page report first. No matter how good the report is, it's not the easiest way to work. This is an opportunity Jev wants to seize: abandon writing long paragraphs of text and let the model return multiple judgments with predefined shapes at once. According to officials, multiple issues can be processed in parallel in the same request; It publishes a service response time of approximately 70-500 ms。Product DocumentationThe method of asking questions in parallel is explained.Release NotesThe velocity range is given. The price quoted when TypeSafe is released is per million input tokens 0.042 USDThe output is not charged separately per token. The token here can be simply understood as the unit of input content segmented during billing. Prices and latency will vary depending on the service and usage conditions. You can't use Jev's one-time categorization fee to directly compare the cost of writing a long article with a chat model. The two do different jobs. The official report showed the highest approximate 193.6 times faster, 444.6 times cheaperThe workflow comparison, while also admitting that these figures may be at the high end of actual revenue. Its evaluation uses multiple complex workflows and refers to the average answers of two other large models, rather than having independently manually verified standard answers to all questions. The testing process is designed by our company.evaluation methodandCompany's Explanation of RestrictionsIt's worth watching in a row. Therefore, the safer conclusion is:This interface demonstrates significant efficiency potential in tasks suitable for breaking down into a large number of small judgments; The exact amount of savings needs to be measured using your own business data. Even if you don't talk nonsense, you need to break it down and understand it.TypeSafe claims that Jev does not produce type errors. For developers, this means that if the pre-defined answer can only be "billing, after-sales service, technical support," the model will not suddenly return a department name that the program does not recognize. This reduces format checking and retries, which is indeed valuable. ButThe format must be correct, but that doesn't necessarily mean the content is correct.。 If the customer actually encounters a bank card pre-authorization, the model may still judge it as a duplicate charge. It may also be overconfident due to the lack of trading status in the input. When discussing "no hallucinations," the official team mainly emphasizes limited output and the inability to generate values outside the range. The reader should not read it as "not misjudging".Type guarantee and evaluation notes in the official descriptionThis separate understanding is also necessary. A truly reliable customer service process should have a clear division of labor: the model judges the intent and urgency of the letter; Procedures verify orders and rules; If you have any doubts, hand them over to someone else; Refund execution retains authorization and records. This way, even if the model makes a mistake once, it won't directly turn into an erroneous payment. Why is it called System One? Will it replace the chat model?"System One" borrows from the psychological contrast between "fast, intuitive judgment" and "slow, cautious thinking". TypeSafe uses it to name its model categories; Jev is named after economist William Stanley Jevons, and the company uses it to express the expectation that as intelligent judgment becomes cheaper, people may use it in more places.See the end of the release notes for the origin of the naming。 This is a product positioning and analogy, and does not mean that Jev's internal mechanisms are equal to human intuition. I prefer to think of it as a new tool next to the chat model. Writing reassuring emails, explaining complex policies, and studying an unprecedented dispute still requires models and people who can organize language and conduct analysis. A lot of repetitive classification, scoring, routing, and verification might be more suitable for an interface like Jev. Actual systems can also combine the two: one is responsible for drafting, the other is responsible for determining whether it should be transferred to manual labor, and finally the program executes clear rules. Perhaps what really deserves attention is how the software is written. In the past, programmers had to force many edge situations into if； Later, they tried to let the chat model handle the entire process. Jev demonstrates a middle ground: **Let the model answer small, well-defined questions, leaving actions, permissions, and safeguards in the code. Whether it can become a general practice depends on accuracy, how probability performs in real business, long-term prices, and whether developers can break down complex problems just right. If you want to judge whether Jev is useful, you don't need to ask first whether it is "the next ChatGPT". Take out a judgment in your software that is repeated thousands of times a day, requires some comprehension, but has a limited range of answers: Who should the complaint be distributed to? Is the invoice missing any materials? Which work orders should be reviewed by someone first? Compare accuracy, latency, total cost, and misjudgment costs using a batch of old cases with artificial conclusions. The answer will be closer to what you really need to know than any "two hundred times faster" sentence. Finally, in layman's termsJev can be understood as a very fast AI sorter or referee: you give it a situation and a few limited options, and it doesn't write a long answer. It only tells you "which one to choose, how many points to give, and whether it is true or not," and then the software continues to execute according to the results. Traditional generative AI is mainly responsible for writing out text, while Jev is mainly responsible for providing small judgments that the software can be used directly. The former is better suited to interpreting, creating, and dealing with open-ended questions, while the latter is better suited to hiding in the background and dealing with decisions with a lot of repetition and a clear range of answers. Written on September 20, 2026. The figures regarding price, speed, and performance in this article are all from publicly available materials from TypeSafe at the time; Customer service emails and forms are illustrative examples of the principles and are not independent tests.

entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-09-21: Global tightening coupled with energy risks, China and the US turn to crisis management | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeThe clearest common theme over the past 24 hours has been a further shift in global policy from "supporting growth" to "controlling risks". The Federal Reserve, the European Central Bank, and the Bank of Japan have all recently adopted a hawkish stance, with interest rates and exchange rates once again becoming core constraints on asset pricing. China maintained the LPR unchanged despite external interest rate differential pressures, while allowing the yuan to appreciate more rapidly, providing a more stable financial backdrop for the meeting between the Chinese and US leaders this week. Similar changes have occurred in technological competition: China and the United States have begun discussing AI national security incident notification mechanisms, extending the competition to crisis management; Meanwhile, traceable shipping in the Strait of Hormuz remains far below pre-war levels, and energy risks continue to influence monetary policy through inflation expectations. The market is no longer facing a single event, but a mutually reinforcing combination of interest rates, exchange rates, AI competition, and the energy supply chain.
Five key news items1. Global interest rate hike expectations have resurfaced, causing the yen to fall to around 156 and triggering intervention warnings.On September 21, during the Asian session, the yen was trading at approximately 156.64 against the US dollar, having fallen by about 2% over the past week. The Bank of Japan raised its policy interest rate to 1.25% last Friday, the highest in 31 years, but two committee members opposed the rate hike, and the lack of strong enough guidance to continue tightening after the meeting put pressure on the yen. Japanese media subsequently reported that authorities conducted an "exchange rate inquiry," a move typically seen by traders as a warning before actual foreign exchange intervention. Meanwhile, the Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank have also raised interest rates this month, and the Fed's hawkish signals pushed the dollar index up more than 1% last week, raising the probability of the market pricing in another rate hike in October to about 55%. This means that global funding costs are rising in tandem, and Japan's single interest rate hike is insufficient to offset the pressure on relative interest rate differentials. Going forward, attention should be paid to whether the Japanese Ministry of Finance has actually entered the market, the trend of US Treasury yields, and whether the Bank of Japan can establish a more credible expectation of continuous tightening.Reuters 2. China's LPR remained unchanged for the 16th consecutive month, with room for easing constrained by external interest rates and bank interest rate spreads.China's loan prime rate remained unchanged in September: the 1-year LPR remained at 3.00%, and the 5-year LPR remained at 3.50%, marking the 16th consecutive month without adjustment. All 21 market participants surveyed by Reuters had previously expected nothing to change. The policy implication is not simply "no need for stimulus," but rather that central banks need to weigh down domestic demand, exchange rates, and the profits of financial institutions. Following the Federal Reserve's recent interest rate hikes, the spread between the yields on 10-year US and Chinese Treasury bonds is hovering near a record high, and further interest rate cuts may increase capital flows and exchange rate pressures. Banks' low net interest margins, coupled with contracting credit demand related to real estate and local governments, have weakened the effect of traditional interest rate cuts on credit expansion. Market institutions therefore believe that China has entered the latter stage of this round of interest rate cut cycles. The key questions going forward are whether domestic demand and the real estate market will weaken further in the fourth quarter, whether inflation can continue to rise, and whether the central bank will rely more on structural tools, liquidity injection, and fiscal synergy to support growth.Reuters 3. The yuan broke through 6.70 to a three-and-a-half-year high, with exchange rate constraints easing ahead of the meeting between the Chinese and US leaders.On September 21, the onshore yuan rose to 6.6957 against the US dollar, its strongest level since January 2023; The offshore yuan is also around 6.695. The People's Bank of China set the central parity rate at 6.7487 that day. Although it was still weaker than market model estimates, the deviation between the central parity rate and market expectations narrowed significantly this month, indicating that the efforts to curb the rapid appreciation of the RMB over the past year are weakening. The timing is particularly noteworthy: U.S. Treasury Secretary Besant and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng have just concluded consultations in New York, and Trump and*are expected to discuss trade, AI, supply chains, and the situation in the Middle East this week. A moderate strengthening of the RMB can help reduce the controversy over "competitive devaluation" and also reduce import costs. However, the interest rate differential between China and the United States is still large, and the domestic fundamentals have not yet been fully reassessed. Therefore, it cannot be simply extrapolated to a long-term unilateral appreciation. Let's look at the summit outcomes, the daily central parity rate deviation, the foreign exchange settlement behavior of export companies, and the US dollar index.Reuters 4. The US and China have proposed an AI national security incident notification mechanism, adding a "crisis management" layer to technological competition.U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said after meeting with He Lifeng in New York on September 20 that the U.S. proposed establishing a China-U.S. AI security briefing mechanism with the goal of increasing transparency when AI-related incidents escalate to the national security level and promoting bilateral AI dialogue that had not been formally established before. The two sides also discussed finalizing the arrangements reached in May and exploring tariff reductions for some non-strategic goods; The current trade truce arrangement will expire on November 10. The fact that export controls on advanced AI chips and semiconductor equipment were not included in this mechanism discussion indicates that potential cooperation is closer to "preventing accidents from escalating" than to eliminating technological competition. If the mechanism is endorsed by the leaders of both countries, it could become a technological risk buffer similar to a crisis hotline, and future issues could involve critical infrastructure, cyberattacks, and AI weaponization. Going forward, attention should be paid to whether this week's summit will formally approve it, how the notification threshold will be defined, and whether export control and tariff negotiations can be advanced in parallel with the security dialogue.Reuters 5. Only 12 vessels were traceable to Hormuz over the weekend; energy transportation risks continue to support inflation premiums.Surface shipping activity in the Strait of Hormuz remains at an extremely low level. Shipping data shows that only 12 trackable cargo ships passed through the strait over the past weekend, down from 35 the previous weekend; Before the outbreak of the US-Israel war with Iran on February 28, this waterway, which carries about one-fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas transportation, typically saw about 125 large merchant ships pass through it daily. Actual oil flows did not collapse proportionally because some Middle Eastern oil tankers shut down their transponders, and Saudi Arabia's crude oil exports in September had recovered from a low of 2.4 million barrels per day in August to more than 4 million barrels per day. However, the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's east-west oil pipeline have forced more crude oil to rely on the strait again, increasing logistics concentration. The risks therefore include not only spot shortages, but also insurance, freight, and premiums for tail supply disruptions. Going forward, we need to observe the opening of the Strait, alternative routes to Saudi Arabia, Brent oil prices, and progress in US-Iran diplomacy.Reuters Market Correlation and Today's ObservationThe most important thing to grasp today is that the four chains of "tightening - exchange rate - energy - technology valuation" are intersecting. On the interest rate side, the Federal Reserve, the European Central Bank, and the Bank of Japan have all been hawkish recently, and the global risk-free interest rate has shifted upward, increasing the valuation discount pressure on long-term growth assets. The yield on the 2-year U.S. Treasury note has risen 36 basis points to about 4.76% in the past two weeks. If expectations for another rate hike in October continue to strengthen, the dollar and U.S. Treasury yields may remain strong, and global risk appetite will rely more on earnings realization than liquidity expansion. On the exchange rate side, there was a clear divergence: the yen weakened even with interest rate hikes, indicating that relative interest rate spreads and policy credibility are more important than a single move; The RMB's rise above 6.70 is more like a combined result of changes in policy tolerance and expectations of stability before the summit, rather than a shift in domestic monetary policy. On the commodity side, Brent crude oil fell by about 2% to around $101 per barrel during the Asian session, indicating that the recovery of actual oil flows could temporarily reduce the risk premium. However, the Hormuz navigation system remained highly abnormal, and the risk of tail supply had not disappeared. If energy prices rise again, it will strengthen the case for continued tightening by European and American central banks and squeeze corporate profits through transportation, chemical and aviation costs. On the technological side, the China-US AI notification mechanism means that the two countries have begun to try to set up guardrails for high-risk technology competition; Meanwhile, Chinese regulators are raising the review threshold for humanoid robot IPOs, focusing on whether the revenue from government-supported projects represents genuine business needs. Unitree rose more than fivefold after its listing before falling 55% from its peak, indicating that highly valued sectors are more sensitive to both interest rates and revenue quality.Reuters Today, the order of observation can be placed on the yields of the US dollar and US Treasury bonds, whether Japan has shifted from verbal warnings to foreign exchange intervention, whether it can hold around 6.70 yuan, whether Brent oil prices have widened the geopolitical premium again, and whether there are new signals about tariffs, AI security, or supply chains before the meeting between the Chinese and US leaders. If energy risks ease and communication between China and the United States improves, risky assets may be given a breather. Conversely, rising oil prices, coupled with expectations of further global interest rate hikes, will directly increase valuation pressure on technology growth stocks, emerging market assets, and highly leveraged industries. Cover image:Peter Beke / Unsplash

entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-09-22: AI Reignites Risk Appetite, US-China Security Dialogue Launched | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeOver the past 24 hours, a striking combination has emerged in the market: global monetary conditions remain tight, but risk assets have strengthened again, driven by the AI investment boom and the decline in oil prices. The U.S. inflation narrative is shifting further from supply shocks such as tariffs and energy to overheated demand, prompting Federal Reserve officials to discuss faster and earlier interest rate hikes. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq hit a new closing high, and AMD's market capitalization reached $1 trillion for the first time, indicating that AI capital spending is still sufficient to offset some interest rate pressures. More specific risk management arrangements have emerged in Sino-US relations, with both sides agreeing to establish a formal AI security dialogue and planning to meet again in Shenzhen in about two months. The cooling down of humanoid robot IPOs in China also indicates that policies are distinguishing between "supporting strategic technologies" and "curbing valuation bubbles". On the energy side, although expensive alternatives have been found for the Hormuz transportation system, costs and geopolitical tail risks still exist.
Five key news items1. Federal Reserve officials say overheated demand is joining inflation-driven growth, and interest rate hikes may need to be implemented more quickly.Chicago Fed President Goolsby said in London on September 21 that U.S. inflation over the past 18 months was initially mainly driven by supply shocks such as tariffs and oil prices, but there is now growing evidence that strong demand is also driving up prices, especially the boom in AI investment and persistently high service sector inflation. He pointed out that if the main theme of inflation shifts to overheated demand, the Federal Reserve's interest rate response will need to be "more aggressive and proactive." The Federal Reserve raised its policy interest rate by 25 basis points last week, the first rate hike in three years; PCE remained at 3.7% year-on-year in July, significantly higher than the 2% target. The policy statement also no longer emphasized specific supply shocks such as energy, but only stated that "inflation remains high." This means that the market can no longer simply assume that a drop in oil prices will cause the Federal Reserve to quickly turn dovish. The focus going forward will be on service inflation, whether AI capital spending will continue to drive aggregate demand, and whether employment and price data ahead of the October meeting will support another interest rate hike.Reuters 2. Nasdaq hits closing record, AMD's market capitalization surpasses $1 trillion for the first time, and AI trading rebounds rapidly.U.S. stocks rebounded significantly on Monday, with the Nasdaq hitting a record close, the S&P 500 rising 1.49%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rising 0.71%. The core driving force is once again coming from AI and semiconductors: AMD rose about 10%, and its market capitalization reached $1 trillion for the first time; Intel rose 12.2%, Arm rose 17%, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index as a whole rose 4.3%. Meanwhile, the yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury note fell below 5%, Brent crude oil fell to an 11-day low, and Bitcoin rose more than 6%, all of which improved risk appetite. The significance of this rise lies in the fact that it occurred just after the Federal Reserve resumed raising interest rates, indicating that investors still believe that AI capital spending and earnings growth can partially offset the higher discount rate. However, the market is still pricing in another interest rate hike in October at around 50%, so the contradiction between valuation expansion and rising interest rates has not been resolved. The next step depends on whether chip orders and cloud vendor capital expenditures can be fulfilled, as well as the valuation resilience of AI leaders if US Treasury yields rise again.Reuters 3. China and the US have formally established an AI security dialogue, and will meet again in Shenzhen in about two months to discuss the "incident hotline".U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessenter said on September 21 that senior Chinese and U.S. officials will meet again in Shenzhen in about two months to continue discussing the risks of artificial intelligence and communication agreements in the event of an AI security incident. Previously, Besant met with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng, and both sides agreed to establish a formal AI dialogue, including an "incident line" for communicating security incidents. Future discussions may cover issues that both sides believe pose systemic risks, such as runaway AI agents and non-state cyber actors. Compared to the previous day's disclosure of only the mechanism proposed by the US, the new development this time is that both sides have agreed to formalize dialogue and determine the direction of the next round of talks. Meanwhile, the US-China tariff truce is set to expire on November 10, but neither side has yet explicitly agreed to an extension. This mechanism will not eliminate chip export controls and technological competition, but it may reduce the probability of AI incidents being misjudged as state acts. We will then observe the specific departments involved in the Shenzhen meeting, the definition of an accident, and the reporting thresholds, as well as whether this week's meeting between the heads of state will grant this mechanism a higher level of political confirmation.Reuters 4. China tightens the pace of humanoid robot IPOs, shifting regulatory focus from technology stories to revenue quality.Reuters reported on September 21 that Chinese regulators are slowing the wave of humanoid robot companies going public, focusing on whether revenue from high valuations and local government-backed projects truly represents business demand. Sources familiar with the matter said that some companies have received informal "window guidance," significantly raising the IPO approval threshold in the industry. One of the key factors triggering regulatory caution was that Unitree’s stock price rose more than fivefold after its IPO, and then fell 55% from its peak. Regulators also pay special attention to robotic data acquisition centers and local government joint ventures, with local government funding accounting for 80% to 90% of the initial investment in some projects. Some investors estimate that if related revenue is excluded, the valuation of some robotics companies may decline by 60% to 70%. This does not mean that Beijing is withdrawing its strategic support for "embodied intelligence," but rather that the policy goal is shifting from expanding financing to verifying orders, deployment scale, and sustainable revenue. Looking ahead, we will see the pace of review for companies planning to go public, actual industrial orders, and whether local government fiscal support will be reduced.Reuters 5. The Hormuz "sea relay" maintains crude oil exports, but VLCC freight rates have exceeded $30 per barrel.Middle Eastern oil-producing countries are using ship-to-ship transshipment to maintain Hormuz exports. Kpler data shows that crude oil exports via Hormuz recovered to about 6.5 million barrels per day in September, the highest level since the brief easing in June. It is estimated that approximately 2.5 million barrels per day of crude oil will be loaded and unloaded via Gulf of Oman vessels this month, up from 1.4 million barrels per day in August, which is equivalent to about 40% of the current crude oil flow in the Strait. This system reduces the risk of a single tanker repeatedly passing through conflict zones, but significantly increases costs: LSEG data shows that the benchmark VLCC freight rate from the Gulf to China has exceeded $30 per barrel, a record high. At the same time, the number of trackable vessels remained far lower than before the war, as many ships turned off their transponders and sailed under American escort. The market is therefore not facing a simple "supply disruption or continuous supply", but rather a coexistence of supply recovery and soaring logistics costs. Going forward, attention should be paid to ship-to-ship transshipment capacity, insurance and freight rates, the recovery of the Saudi East-West oil pipeline, and whether any ceasefire negotiations can truly reduce the risk premium.Reuters Market Correlation and Today's ObservationThe core of asset pricing today is that "the growth narrative has once again overshadowed the tightening narrative, but the two are colliding head-on." On the interest rate side, Federal Reserve officials have begun to explicitly discuss overheated demand, indicating that even if oil prices fall from their highs, service prices and AI investments may still keep inflation sticky. If the probability of a rate hike in October continues to rise, short-term US Treasury bonds will come under pressure again. On the exchange rate side, the US dollar remains supported by high interest rates, while after the RMB previously broke through 6.70, the market will continue to observe whether the People's Bank of China's central parity rate will allow for further appreciation before the meeting between the Chinese and US leaders. In terms of risk appetite, the Nasdaq hitting a new high, AMD entering the trillion-dollar market capitalization bracket, and Bitcoin's rise indicate that funds are chasing high-beta assets again. However, this market is highly dependent on yields and should not rise rapidly again. The commodity market provided a buffer: the continuous decline in crude oil alleviated immediate inflation anxieties, but the real structure of Hormuz has not returned to normal. Exports of 6.5 million barrels per day and large-scale ship-to-ship transshipment demonstrate the resilience of the supply chain, while VLCC transportation costs exceeding $30 per barrel mean that geopolitical risks are shifting from "quantity shortages" to "logistics taxes". In terms of Chinese policy, the cooling of humanoid robot IPOs is worth considering alongside the rise in US AI stocks: both capital markets recognize long-term investment in AI, but regulators and investors are beginning to pay more attention to revenue quality, real orders, and safety responsibilities. Today, the focus should be on whether US Treasury yields can maintain their decline, whether oil prices will continue to fall, whether the rally in AI semiconductors can spread, and whether new enforceable arrangements for the trade truce and AI security mechanisms will emerge before the US-China summit. If yields and oil prices fall simultaneously, technology valuations will still have support; If evidence of demand-driven inflation strengthens, current risk appetite may again face pressure from higher interest rates. Cover image:Daniel Brzdęk / Unsplash

entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-09-23: AI Regulation Heats Up, Sino-European Auto Investment and Hormuz Risks Go Hand in Hand | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeThe common theme over the past 24 hours has been that global growth and technology investment are still moving forward, but policies are beginning to price risks more clearly. On the one hand, AI is shifting from a "model competition" to payment, copyright, and financial data security: European and American tech companies want Australia to relax restrictions on training data, while global banks are demanding clearer responsibilities and consumer protections for proxy shopping. China's foreign economic policy has further directed competition in the automotive industry towards local European investment in order to cope with tariffs and upcoming increased localization requirements. Geopolitically, Iran has offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, while the United States has maintained high pressure and confirmed that communication is continuing. For the market, interest rates, energy logistics, AI capital expenditures, and trade rules are simultaneously determining the risk premium.
Five key news items1. Global banks warn AI shopping agents are amplifying fraud and data risks, and payment rules are facing rewriting.On September 22, several global banks issued warnings about the rapidly expanding "proxy business". NatWest, Bank of America, ING, Capital One, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, and ASB New Zealand, among others, point out that existing regulatory, anti-fraud, and liability mechanisms may not keep up with the pace of technology when AI agents search, select, and even complete payments for consumers. Risks include not only model recommendation bias, but also mishandling of sensitive financial data, agents choosing less secure payment methods, and fraudsters using automated processes to amplify fraud. There has been a significant change on the demand side: John Lewis' search traffic from AI tools in the UK has increased from about 0.3% to 2.5% within a year. Banks advocate for at least establishing clear disclosure, data protection, explainable decision-making, and consumer recourse mechanisms for AI participation in transactions. Its importance lies in the fact that AI is moving from "answering questions" to actually executing fund instructions, and the targets of financial regulation are expanding from people and institutions to software agents. It remains to be seen whether major payment networks, bank regulators, and technology platforms can form a unified framework for identity authentication, authorization, and compensation.Reuters 2. OpenAI and Anthropic are demanding that Australia relax AI training restrictions and link copyright to data center investment.In submissions to the Australian Parliament's Joint Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence, OpenAI and Anthropic urged the government to reconsider its position on prohibiting the unauthorized use of Australian copyrighted content to train AI models. Instead of demanding a blanket exemption, the two companies advocated for the establishment of limited, conditional training exceptions to strike a balance between creator rights and model development. Australia plans to push for more comprehensive AI regulation next year, but the government has previously ruled out changes to the copyright system and broad exemptions for training data. The debate is also linked to infrastructure investment: OpenAI is working with NextDC on a Sydney data center project, and Anthropic is also involved in related data center collaborations in Queensland. For Australia, this is no longer a simple copyright issue, but a policy trade-off between local content industry revenue, computing power investment, energy demand, and the competitiveness of the AI industry. The committee is expected to submit its report in November, and should focus on whether there are narrow exceptions to text and data mining, licensing payment mechanisms, and whether data center investment has been included in policy negotiations.Reuters 3. China supports automakers investing in Europe, with local production becoming a new path to addressing EU trade barriers.Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao said on September 22 that China supports Chinese automakers' investment in Europe and hopes to resolve disputes in the automotive industry through the China-EU economic and trade consultation mechanism based on the principles of compliance, balance and non-discrimination. He previously met with Hildegard Mueller, President of the German Association of the Automotive Industry, and had a video conference with Ola Källenius, CEO of Mercedes-Benz and President of the European Automobile Manufacturers Association. The backdrop is that the EU has imposed additional tariffs of up to 35.3% on Chinese-made pure electric vehicles, while simultaneously developing stronger local production requirements; China's plug-in hybrid electric vehicles are currently not covered by the aforementioned additional tariffs on pure electric vehicles, making exports a new policy focus. Beijing's encouragement of local European investment signifies that industrial competition is shifting from simple exports to factories, supply chains, and R&D locations. For Europe, this could bring capital and jobs, but it could also intensify competition among local brands. The subsequent focus will be on the EU's local content rules, hybrid vehicle trade measures, and the speed of Chinese automakers' location selection and supply chain localization in Europe.Reuters 4. Volkswagen expects the Chinese passenger vehicle market to shrink by approximately 20% in 2026, with domestic demand and price competition intensifying.Ralf Brandstaetter, head of Volkswagen China, said at an industry summit on September 22 that the size of the Chinese passenger vehicle market is expected to decline by about 20% in 2026, describing the current level of contraction as close to the impact of the pandemic. China's domestic auto sales had declined year-on-year for 11 consecutive months as of August, but auto exports remained strong during the same period, forming a clear divergence between "weak domestic demand and strong overseas expansion". For Volkswagen, China remains one of the most important markets. The simultaneous decline in sales and narrowing profit margins also reflects greater pressure on traditional joint venture brands in terms of new energy vehicle models, software capabilities, and price competition. At the macro level, automobiles are an important component of China's durable goods consumption, manufacturing investment, and local industrial chains. Continued contraction will increase the urgency of policies to promote consumption and industry consolidation. On the other hand, export growth will increase trade frictions between China and Europe. It remains to be seen whether consumption support policies such as trade-in programs will be strengthened, whether the price war among automakers will ease, and whether exports can continue to absorb excess domestic capacity.Reuters 5. Iran sets conditions for reopening Hormuz within seven days, simultaneously signaling high-pressure US-Iran negotiations.On September 22, a senior Iranian official said that Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the United States reduces military pressure and lifts the blockade of Iranian ports. Iran stated that a plan to end hostilities was submitted to the United States through intermediaries on September 16. On the same day, US President Trump publicly called on other countries to impose complete economic isolation on Iran at the UN General Assembly, but later stated that the US and Iran were still communicating that day and believed that an arrangement could eventually be reached. Before the war, the Strait carried about one-fifth of the world's oil and gas transportation, so any verifiable reopening path would directly affect crude oil, shipping, and inflation expectations. France has also begun pushing the UN Security Council to discuss an international mission to resume navigation through the Strait, indicating that energy security is returning to the multilateral diplomatic agenda. The current signals are still contradictory and cannot be considered as an imminent ceasefire; The key questions going forward are whether the United States responds to Iran's conditions, whether the port blockade is adjusted, whether the actual shipping flow in the strait increases, and whether the negotiations can shift from indirect contact to an enforceable agreement.Reuters Market Correlation and Today's ObservationToday's asset pricing can be observed along five lines: interest rates, energy, risk appetite, technology valuations, and China policies. In terms of interest rates, energy supply remains a significant source of tail risk to global inflation: if there is a verifiable resumption of navigation in Hormuz, oil prices and shipping insurance premiums are expected to decline, thereby alleviating the reflationary pressures faced by major central banks. If negotiations break down and energy prices rise again, it will squeeze the room for interest rate cuts and push up long-term yields. In terms of exchange rates, the US dollar will still be driven by both US interest rate expectations and safe-haven demand, while the currencies of energy-importing countries are more sensitive to changes in oil prices. The contradiction between risk appetite and technology valuation is more structured. AI investment continues to drive demand for data centers, chips, and cloud computing, but bank warnings about the risks of AI agent payments and copyright disputes in Australia indicate that regulatory costs will rise along with revenue opportunities once commercialization enters real transactions. In China, weak domestic demand for automobiles and companies accelerating their investment in Europe are two sides of the same coin: domestic price competition and insufficient demand have prompted automakers to seek growth overseas, while European tariffs and localization rules have forced the export model to shift to capital and production capacity going global. Today, we should focus on observing the actual shipping flow and oil prices in Hormuz, long-term interest rates between China, the US, and Europe, the trend of the US dollar, and changes in European rules for investing in Chinese automobiles. If energy risks ease, the market may re-increase its valuation tolerance for growth assets; If oil prices and interest rates rise simultaneously, overvalued technology and highly leveraged industries will be the first to come under pressure. Cover image:Sam Jotham Sutharson / Unsplash

entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-09-24: Obstacles cleared ahead of the US-China summit, interest rate and energy risks intertwined | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeOver the past 24 hours, the main theme of global markets has shifted from simply chasing AI growth to simultaneously repricing policy and geopolitical risks. Ahead of the summit between the two leaders on September 24, China and the United States continued to address "unfinished business" such as the trade truce and tariffs on rare earths and non-strategic goods. Both countries expressed their willingness to maintain strategic stability, but specific arrangements still need to be finalized. The People's Bank of China announced that it would replenish liquidity with overnight reverse repos of up to 1 trillion yuan per day before the National Day and Mid-Autumn Festival holidays, with a focus on smoothing funding needs at the end of the quarter and during long holidays, rather than changing the direction of interest rates. In the United States, expectations of further interest rate hikes pushed the dollar to a near two-month high; The popularity of AI applications continues to support technology risk appetite, but oil prices, bond yields, and the situation in the Middle East have amplified valuation volatility again. Iran has proposed reopening the Strait of Hormuz within seven days of the U.S. reducing military pressure and lifting the port blockade, providing a new diplomatic observation window for energy risks.
Five key news items1. "Unfinished business" discussed again ahead of the US-China summit; trade truce and rare earth elements remain key variables.U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessenter said on September 23 that he met again with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in Washington that day to address the "unfinished business" left behind in Sunday's consultations and prepare for Trump's meeting with*on September 24. The nearly one-year trade truce between the two sides will expire on November 10; The previous truce had significantly reduced bilateral tariffs, which had once risen to triple digits, and China had also agreed to restore supplies of rare earth magnets and other key minerals. U.S. Trade Representative Greer previously stated that the two sides are also advancing the "Trade Commission" mechanism agreed upon in May to explore reducing some tariffs on consumer goods, low-tech products, and non-strategic goods such as U.S. energy, agricultural products, and medical devices. The current new progress does not mean that a comprehensive agreement has been reached, but rather that technical differences continue to be resolved before the summit. The market should focus on whether the truce will be extended, rare earth compliance standards, Boeing and agricultural product procurement, and whether the tariff list for non-strategic goods can be formulated into an enforceable text.Reuters 2. The People's Bank of China will inject up to 1 trillion yuan per day before the National Day and Mid-Autumn Festival holidays, focusing on alleviating short-term funding pressures at the end of the quarter.On September 23, the People's Bank of China announced that it would conduct overnight reverse repurchase operations as needed from September 28 to October 8, with a maximum daily scale of RMB 1 trillion, in order to meet the short-term liquidity needs of the banking system. China's interbank bond market will be closed from September 25 to 27 during the Mid-Autumn Festival and from October 1 to 7 during the National Day holiday. Long holidays coinciding with the end of the quarter usually increase the demand for cash, payment settlement and institutional reserves. Therefore, the central bank has provided large-scale short-term liquidity arrangements in advance. At the current exchange rate, 1 trillion yuan is equivalent to approximately $149 billion, but the "maximum amount" does not mean that the full amount will be injected every day, nor can it be directly interpreted as a new aggregate stimulus. Its policy significance lies primarily in reducing abnormal fluctuations in cross-quarter funding rates and avoiding the transmission of short-term liquidity shortages to the bond and credit markets.
