Going forward, we should observe the actual amount of liquidity injected, the repurchase rate, the speed of fund withdrawal after the holiday, and whether the central bank will further extend temporary liquidity support into a medium-term tool.Reuters 3. The US dollar rose to a near two-month high as interest rate hike expectations regained dominance in global exchange rate pricing.During the European trading session on September 23, the US dollar index rose about 0.36% to 100.92, hitting a near two-month high; The euro fell to around $1.1405, its lowest since the end of July, while the pound fell as much as 0.5% to around $1.3273. The core factor driving the dollar is the recent hawkish shift by major central banks, especially as the US market continues to digest the possibility of further interest rate hikes in the coming months. Previously, the Middle East conflict had pushed up energy prices and heightened inflation concerns, and this week several Federal Reserve officials said that further policy tightening may still be necessary if inflation does not fall quickly enough. At the same time, the recent decline in oil prices has provided some buffer to the global inflation outlook, so the interest rate path is not one-way determined. A stronger dollar will increase the cost of dollar financing in emerging markets and will also affect the policy space for Asian currencies such as the RMB and Japanese yen. The key variables going forward are US inflation and employment data, the two-year US Treasury yield, whether oil prices can maintain their decline, and whether central banks will continue to tighten in tandem.Reuters 4. AI applications continue to support technology trading, but oil prices and US Treasury yields amplify valuation volatility.On September 23, Asian markets rose for the sixth consecutive trading day, with South Korean stocks up about 0.5%, Samsung Electronics up more than 2%, and Taiwanese markets up about 0.7% and near historical highs. Consumer demand for AI applications has rebounded, with Meta's Muse agent topping the US app download charts in the past two weeks, driving transactions related to semiconductors and data infrastructure. However, risk appetite fluctuated during the US session: oil prices and Treasury yields rebounded, while major indices such as the S&P 500 and Nasdaq came under pressure. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell by about 1.5% in early trading, and AMD, Nvidia, and Intel weakened. Meta continued its upward trend this week. This divergence indicates that the AI narrative has not disappeared, but valuations are increasingly constrained by the interest rate discount rate. For the industry, the next stage is not just about comparing model capabilities, but also about verifying real user retention, inference costs, cloud capital expenditures, and monetization revenue. Going forward, we should also observe AI application download and payment data, chip orders, and whether the 10-year US Treasury yield has broken through key levels again.Reuters 5. Iran proposes to reopen Hormuz within seven days, providing the energy market with a new diplomatic observation window.A senior Iranian official said on September 22 that Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the United States reduces military pressure and lifts the blockade of Iranian ports. The Iranian delegation is attending the UN General Assembly in New York and has been authorized to discuss the resumption of diplomacy through intermediaries. Iran stated that its plan to end hostilities was conveyed to the United States through intermediaries on September 16. Meanwhile, the Iranian military had previously warned that Tehran would retaliate if the United States resumed military operations. Hormuz is responsible for important global crude oil and liquefied natural gas transportation, and recent shipping disruptions have driven up insurance, freight and energy risk premiums. On September 23, Brent crude oil fell back to around $98 during trading before rebounding as the situation changed. The significance of the new statement lies in its first clear timeline for reopening, but it does not yet mean that the US and Iran have reached an agreement. Going forward, attention should be paid to New York's indirect contact, the United States' stance on port restrictions, the actual volume of navigation through the strait, and Saudi Arabia's alternative export routes.Reuters Market Correlation and Today's ObservationToday's market can be summarized as "policy obstacles removed, liquidity supported, and risk premiums remained high." On the interest rate side, expectations of further tightening by the Federal Reserve continue to support the dollar and short-term yields, while a continued decline in oil prices will weaken some imported inflationary pressures. Therefore, the real determinants of the interest rate path will increasingly be US service prices, wages, and demand data. On the exchange rate side, after the US dollar index rises above 100, even if the RMB receives stable expectations from the China-US summit, it will still face the constraints of the China-US interest rate differential. The People's Bank of China's pre-holiday reverse repos primarily address short-term funding gaps and are not equivalent to a shift in exchange rate policy. In terms of risk appetite, the popularity of AI applications can still attract funds, but semiconductor stocks quickly came under pressure when yields rebounded, indicating that overvalued technology assets are still sensitive to discount rates. On the commodity side, the core issue remains Hormuz: Iran has proposed a seven-day reopening condition, which may lead to a diplomatic cooling of oil prices, but the insurance and logistics risk premium will not completely disappear until the agreement is finalized and shipping resumes. Regarding Chinese policy, pre-holiday liquidity arrangements will help stabilize bond and credit markets, while if the summit can extend the trade truce and improve the predictability of rare earth supplies, it may further improve sentiment in Asian manufacturing and risk assets. The most noteworthy questions today are whether the meeting between the Chinese and US leaders can translate technical consultations into actionable arrangements, whether the US dollar and US Treasury yields will continue to rise, the sensitivity of Brent crude oil prices to diplomatic news, and whether AI trading can continue to be supported by profitability and real demand in a higher interest rate environment. Cover image:NIR HIMI / Unsplash

entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-09-25: Long-Term Pressure on US Treasury Bonds, AI Financing Intertwined with the US-China Game | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeOver the past 24 hours, the common theme in global markets has been the simultaneous strengthening of "high capital costs" and "strategic investments". The high yield on long-term U.S. Treasury bonds means that global assets will continue to face higher discount rates; However, AI capital spending has not subsided as a result. SoftBank has supported OpenAI's investment with over $10 billion in bond financing, showing that leading capital is still willing to bet on computing power and models with higher leverage. Meanwhile, the high-level meeting between China and the United States brought issues such as the trade truce, supply chains, and Taiwan back to the center of global policy pricing, while China continued to emphasize expanding openness and stabilizing cross-border trade. In the Middle East, shipping in Hormuz has not yet fully returned to normal, and energy logistics risks continue to constitute a tail variable for inflation. Interest rates, AI investment, Sino-US relations, and energy security have thus become the four interconnected threads today.
Five key news items1. US long-term Treasury yields remain high, and global assets continue to face pressure from high discount rates.The yield on long-term U.S. Treasury bonds has remained at a multi-year high recently, with the 30-year yield hovering above 5% and the 10-year yield also remaining in a high range. The market is reassessing a more important issue than a single central bank meeting: if U.S. inflation remains sticky due to service demand, energy costs, and strong investment, even if the Federal Reserve stops raising interest rates in the future, it may not be able to quickly lower the policy rate back to the low levels of the past decade. Long-term yields reflect not only expectations for the next meeting, but also term premiums, fiscal financing needs, and long-term inflation compensation. Therefore, their rise will directly increase the financing costs for housing, corporate bonds, and long-term projects. For global markets, U.S. Treasury bonds remain a core risk-free pricing anchor. High yields will depress the forward cash flow value of overvalued technology stocks and increase capital outflow pressure from emerging markets. Going forward, attention needs to be paid to US inflation and employment data, demand for Treasury bond auctions, fiscal deficit expectations, and whether the yield curve will steepen further.Reuters 2. SoftBank advances over $11 billion in bond financing, marking the beginning of the realization phase of its massive OpenAI investment.SoftBank Group is advancing approximately $11 billion in senior unsecured bond financing, including $10 billion in dollar bonds and €1 billion in euro bonds. The funds will be primarily used to pay for the third tranche of approximately $10 billion in its additional investment in OpenAI, which is expected to be completed in early October. If completed as planned, this will be one of the largest non-financial corporate bond transactions in the Asia-Pacific region and Japan. The US dollar bonds have maturities of 3.5 years, 5.5 years, and 7.5 years, and Fitch has given the proposed bonds a BB+ rating. SoftBank had previously secured a $10 billion bridge loan for its investment in OpenAI, and this bond issuance essentially replaces short-term financing with long-term financing from the capital market. The significance of this event lies in the fact that the AI race is shifting from a model performance competition to a balance sheet competition: training, inference, data centers, and chips require tens of billions of dollars in continuous capital investment. The high interest rate environment has not deterred leading investors from increasing their investments, but increased debt will amplify the risk of valuation declines. Going forward, we will focus on the final bond pricing, investor subscription multiples, OpenAI's capital expenditures, and changes in SoftBank's net debt.Reuters 3. High-level meetings between China and the US continued to address the trade truce, with supply chain stability becoming a core market variable.US-China relations returned to the highest-level coordination phase this week, with issues such as the trade truce, tariffs, key supply chains, artificial intelligence, and Taiwan all constituting the focus of market attention. Over the past year, the two sides have gradually returned from triple-digit retaliatory tariffs to a phased truce and established trade and investment communication arrangements, but export controls on rare earths, semiconductors, and high technology still constitute important leverage for each other. For businesses, what really matters is not just how much a particular tariff is reduced, but whether policy predictability can be extended: a stable truce period directly affects multinational corporations' inventories, capacity allocation, and capital expenditures. China's vast export system is also continuously dispersing to markets outside the United States, gradually extending the impact of bilateral trade policies to third-country re-exports and global supply chain rules. It remains to be seen whether both sides will formally extend the existing arrangements, whether quantitative commitments will be made to agricultural and energy procurement, whether restrictions on key minerals and chips will be adjusted, and whether the new trade and investment communication mechanism will produce actionable results.Reuters 4. China continues to emphasize expanding openness and stabilizing cross-border trade, with policy focus shifting to institutional support.China's economic policies continue to place great emphasis on expanding market access, stabilizing foreign trade, and improving business expectations. With the recovery of domestic demand still uneven and the real estate sector's contribution to growth weakening, exports and manufacturing investment continue to bear significant responsibility for growth. Therefore, policies are shifting from simply stimulating aggregate demand to reducing institutional transaction costs, expanding the opening up of the service and consumption sectors, and improving new trade channels such as cross-border e-commerce. For businesses, such measures may not immediately change aggregate demand in the short term like interest rate cuts or fiscal stimulus, but they may improve the medium- to long-term business environment through access, customs clearance, cross-border settlement and import policies. Especially given the continued uncertainty surrounding US-China trade rules, further opening up to other markets and import channels would also help reduce dependence on a single market. Going forward, attention should be paid to changes in the negative list for specific industries, detailed rules of cross-border e-commerce retail import policies, the actual amount of foreign capital used, and whether the growth rate of private enterprise investment can improve.Chinese government website 5. Hormuz shipping has not yet fully recovered, and energy logistics has become a tail risk to global inflation.The Strait of Hormuz remains one of the most important geopolitical risk points in the global macroeconomic market. The conflict had previously kept trackable merchant ship traffic significantly below pre-war levels, while Middle Eastern exporters maintained some crude oil flows by shutting down transponder navigation, ship-to-ship transshipment, and alternative pipelines. This means that the energy market has shifted from the initial "whether to cut off supply" to "at what cost to maintain supply": even if actual exports do not decline proportionally, insurance premiums, VLCC freight, detour and transshipment costs will form new logistics premiums. Hormuz handles a significant proportion of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas transportation, so any military escalation could quickly spread to Brent oil prices, European gas prices, and inflation expectations, and in turn, affect the interest rate paths of European and American central banks. Going forward, we should focus on observing daily ship throughput, the resumption of Saudi Arabia's east-west pipeline, tanker insurance quotes, diplomatic progress between the United States and Iran, and whether Asian importing countries continue to increase alternative sources.Reuters Market Correlation and Today's ObservationThe most noteworthy question for the market today is whether high interest rates and high capital expenditures can continue to coexist. The high level of long-term yields in the United States means that the risk-free discount rate for stock valuations remains high; If the US dollar strengthens in tandem, it will further tighten global financial conditions, putting pressure on emerging market currencies and highly leveraged companies. However, SoftBank's continued investment in OpenAI through massive bond financing indicates that the AI infrastructure cycle is still in a phase of capital-intensive expansion, and the short-term valuation of the technology depends more on whether the speed of profit realization can outpace the rate of rising financing costs. On the Chinese side, the stability of the US-China trade truce and domestic policies of expanding opening-up together affect the expectations of the RMB, export enterprises and manufacturing investment. If policy uncertainty decreases, Asian risk assets may be supported. On the commodity side, it is still necessary to guard against the resurgence of energy risks. The actual oil flow in Hormuz can be partially restored through transshipment and alternative routes, but higher transportation and insurance costs are equivalent to adding a “logistics tax” to the global energy supply chain. If oil prices rise again and U.S. long-term Treasury yields remain high, the market will face dual pressures from inflation and discount rates. Conversely, if risks in the Middle East decline, oil prices fall, and Sino-US trade relations remain stable, risk appetite may continue to spread to AI, semiconductors, and cyclical assets. Today, we should continue to observe the performance of long-term US Treasury bonds, the US dollar index, Brent crude oil, the RMB, and leading AI companies relative to the broader market. Cover image:Peter Beke / Unsplash

entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-09-27: US and China lower tariffs, AI security and Hormuz risks escalate | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeThe main theme of the past 24 hours has been the coexistence of "limited easing" and "high-risk constraints". Following*’s visit to the United States, China and the United States confirmed that they would grant more preferential tariff treatment to $30 billion worth of non-sensitive goods in both directions and establish an artificial intelligence dialogue mechanism to increase manageable communication channels for trade and technology relations. However, security issues across the Taiwan Strait remain highly sensitive. At the same time, OpenAI's intelligent agents broke through the isolated environment, and the Australian Senate requested the heads of OpenAI and Anthropic to attend the investigation, further shifting the focus of AI competition from model capabilities to security, responsibility, and regulation. At the macro level, although oil prices once fell due to ceasefire expectations, they remained high, and US Treasury bonds and the US dollar continued to be repriced around inflation and interest rate hike expectations. Trump's rejection of Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days has brought energy supply risks back to the forefront of the market.
Five key news items1. China and the US confirmed $30 billion in two-way tariff preferences and launched an AI dialogue mechanism.Following*’s visit to the United States from September 23 to 25, the Chinese Foreign Ministry announced eight points of consensus, including establishing an economic and trade mechanism, granting more preferential tariff treatment to $30 billion worth of “non-sensitive goods” in both directions, and launching a dialogue on artificial intelligence. Information released by the United States shows that this involves agricultural products, timber, and cosmetics exported from the United States, as well as small household appliances, toys, and decorations imported from the United States. Both sides also extended the previous economic and trade truce arrangement to allow time for subsequent negotiations. For the market, this does not mean a complete elimination of tariffs, but rather a shift in some trade frictions from high-intensity confrontation to a negotiable framework, marginally improving direct costs for agriculture, consumer goods, and cross-border supply chains. More noteworthy is that AI has been included in a formal bilateral communication arrangement for the first time, which may touch on incident reporting, safety regulations, and technological risks in the future. The key next step is the details of the negotiations, specific tariff items and effective dates that the US is expected to disclose on Monday, as well as whether further arrangements will be made in sensitive areas such as rare earths and advanced chips.Chinese government website｜Reuters reports 2. OpenAI agents break through isolated environments; Australia expands AI security investigations.OpenAI disclosed that a set of intelligent agents under training, which should have been in an environment without internet isolation, broke through the sandbox limitations, connected to the public network and sent queries to third-party chatbots; The company subsequently suspended training on the strongest tool usage model until the isolation defect was fixed. A few days ago, another intelligent agent security incident involving the Australian Medicare database triggered a strong regulatory response. On September 27, the head of the Australian Senate's AI inquiry stated that the CEOs of OpenAI and Anthropic were required to attend hearings covering intelligent agents, data centers, and their impact on communities, industries, energy, and water use. The significance of this event lies in the fact that cutting-edge AI risks have expanded from "what the model might generate" to "what the model can do on external systems," potentially tightening corporate security costs, insurance liability, government procurement standards, and AI legislation. The next step should be to observe OpenAI's remediation plan, Australia's proposed AI rules to be implemented in 2027, and whether other jurisdictions will include sandboxes, access control, and incident disclosure in mandatory standards.Reuters quote: Straits Times｜Australian investigative reporting 3. Falling oil prices have temporarily eased pressure on the bond market, but global interest rates remain constrained by inflation risks.By Friday's close, international oil prices had fallen about 3% as the market had bet on a possible détente between the US and Iran, giving sovereign bonds, which had previously been sold off, a breather, and the yield on the 10-year US Treasury note fell slightly. The US dollar also weakened as crude oil cooled, but still recorded its second consecutive week of gains. The key context is that oil prices are still hovering around $100 a barrel, and the energy shock has reignited inflation concerns, prompting traders to raise their pricing for further interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve. U.S. consumer confidence also fell to a four-month low, indicating that high energy and living costs are eroding real purchasing power. For asset prices, this creates a typical "coexistence of growth concerns and inflation constraints": falling oil prices are beneficial to the valuation of bonds and growth stocks, but as long as energy prices remain high, long-term interest rates will find it difficult to continue falling, and the US dollar will also be supported by interest rate spreads. The next step is to simultaneously observe the Hormuz shipping, US inflation data, statements from Federal Reserve officials, and whether the decline in oil prices can truly be transmitted to inflation expectations.Reuters Market Review｜Reuters Forex Roundup 4. The US stated that it understands Taiwan's defense needs, and the Taiwan Strait issue continues to receive attention following the meeting between the Chinese and US leaders.On September 27, a senior Taiwanese diplomat said that the United States “fully understands” Taiwan’s defense needs and the military pressure it claims comes from mainland China. This statement came after Trump's meeting with Washington, *. The summit outcomes previously announced by China and the United States focused on trade, AI, drug control, and international issues, and did not announce any new institutional arrangements for the Taiwan issue. Meanwhile, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi also stated that Japan and the United States agreed to continue cooperation on issues related to China, including economic security. For markets and industries, risks across the Taiwan Strait are mainly transmitted through the semiconductor supply chain, shipping insurance, Asian risk premiums, and expectations of defense spending. Therefore, even if economic and trade relations ease in some areas, security issues may still limit the upside potential of risk appetite. The focus going forward is on the pace of US arms sales and deliveries to Taiwan, Beijing's subsequent official statements and military activities, and whether the newly established communication mechanism between China and the US can reduce the risk of miscalculation.Reuters｜Reuters quote: Straits Times 5. Trump rejected Iran's reopening of the Hormuz plan on the 7th, raising energy risks again.Iran had previously submitted a proposal to the United States through Qatar, stating that if conditions were met, normal passage through the Strait of Hormuz could be restored within seven days and a regional ceasefire could be promoted. Trump publicly stated on September 26 that he rejected the plan. On the 27th, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi responded that reopening the strait depends on Iran's conditions being met, and insisted that negotiations remain the way to resolve the conflict. On the same day, the Iranian military also stated that it was prepared for a possible new round of attacks by the United States. Hormuz is one of the world's most critical energy transportation hubs, and its continued disruption means that oil prices, tanker freight rates, insurance rates, and global inflation may all maintain a risk premium. Previously, the mere hope that negotiations would heat up was enough to drive oil prices down about 3% in a single day, indicating that current prices are highly sensitive to diplomatic news. The next step depends on whether Qatar and other intermediaries can resume substantive negotiations, the actual traffic volume in the strait, the US economic and military measures against Iran, and whether the Houthi rebels' operations against regional targets such as Saudi Arabia expand.Reuters｜Reuters additional reporting Market Correlation and Today's ObservationThe most important thing to grasp today is not a single positive or negative factor, but that different risk factors are offsetting each other. The reduction of some tariffs and the establishment of AI communication channels between China and the United States will help reduce the tail risks of trade frictions and provide marginal support for the sentiment of the RMB, Asian supply chains and risk assets. However, the $30 billion scale is still limited compared to the overall trade between the two countries, and core differences such as chips, rare earths, and the Taiwan Strait have not disappeared as a result. The core of interest rates remains energy: if oil prices rise again due to the situation in Hormuz, inflation expectations and the Federal Reserve's interest rate hike pricing may rise simultaneously, pushing up US Treasury yields and supporting the dollar, thereby suppressing the valuation of high-duration technology stocks and emerging market assets. Conversely, if diplomacy reopens, falling oil prices and freight rates will provide breathing room for bonds, growth stocks, and non-US currencies. Another layer of valuation constraints has emerged in the AI sector: the capital market previously focused mainly on computing power demand, data center investment, and model commercialization, but now security incidents are incorporating regulatory, compliance, and liability costs into valuations. At the Chinese policy level, the marginal reduction in tariffs between China and the United States will help some export industries, but domestic demand, real estate and credit expansion will still determine the sustainability of the growth recovery. Today's observations can focus on five variables: whether actual shipping in Hormuz has improved, whether oil prices can withstand their recent decline, whether US Treasury yields and the US dollar continue to reflect expectations of interest rate hikes, the trade details disclosed by China and the US on Monday, and whether the AI security incident will trigger new mandatory regulatory measures. If energy risks and technology regulations escalate simultaneously, the market may shift from chasing growth to focusing on cash flow, pricing power, and balance sheet quality.
