entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-09-28: Oil Prices Rebound, AI Regulation and Geopolitical Risks Heat Up Again | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeThe common theme over the past 24 hours has been that both policies and the market are repricing "technological capability spillover and the prolongation of geopolitical conflicts." After Trump rejected Iran's peace proposal, expectations for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz cooled rapidly, Brent crude rose back to around $106 a barrel, and energy inflation once again became a constraint on interest rates and risk assets. The technology sector has also shifted from pursuing capabilities to controlling risks: the Australian Senate has demanded that the heads of OpenAI and Anthropic be questioned regarding the AI agent overreach incident; China is reportedly considering conditionally allowing some companies to purchase Nvidia's professional chips, indicating that it is seeking a more delicate balance between its independent and controllable goals and actual computing power needs. Meanwhile, the Swiss referendum left room for sanctions and NATO cooperation, and Russia expanded its strikes on Ukrainian cities and communications infrastructure, indicating that security policies, supply chains, and capital costs are becoming increasingly intertwined.
Five key news items1. The US rejected the Iran peace plan, causing international oil prices to jump again.In early Asian trading on September 28, international oil prices rebounded by more than 1% after Trump rejected a peace proposal from Iran. As of 22:02 GMT, Brent crude oil rose $1.82 to $106.14 a barrel, or 1.74%. U.S. WTI rose $1.14 to $93.55, a gain of 1.23%. The Iranian plan reportedly involves ending the conflict and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a shipping lane that carries a significant amount of global crude oil and liquefied natural gas trade. Therefore, any expected opening or blockade would quickly translate into freight rates, insurance, and refined oil prices. Previously, the market had bet on diplomatic détente, which led to a decline in oil prices and long-term government bond yields. This rejection means that the risk premium has returned to the energy curve. For the global economy, persistently high oil prices will raise transportation, agriculture, and manufacturing costs and limit the room for major central banks to shift to easing. The next steps should be to observe whether Iran proposes a revised plan, the actual volume of navigation through Hormuz, whether the United States will resume military operations, and whether Brent can hold above $105.Reuters 2. China is considering allowing ByteDance and Alibaba to purchase professional chips from Nvidia.On September 27, Reuters, citing The Information, reported that The Chinese government has signaled that it may allow companies such as ByteDance and Alibaba to purchase Nvidia's RTX PRO 5500 chips for high-end professional computers. The report indicates that the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology recently required relevant companies to submit procurement plans and expressed its preference for approval to some companies; Industry insiders expect the product may circumvent current U.S. export restrictions. However, Reuters has not yet independently verified this, and the Chinese government and the two companies did not immediately respond, so it should currently be regarded as a policy assessment rather than a formal release. Its importance lies in the fact that, on the one hand, Beijing continues to promote the independence of domestically produced computing power and supply chain; on the other hand, domestic large-scale model training, inference, and content services still require high-performance hardware that can be immediately deployed. If the approval is granted, it will restore some of Nvidia's revenue in China and may also improve the computing power bottleneck of internet platforms. However, the scope of procurement, use review, and domestic substitution requirements can all be very strict. Going forward, we will pay attention to the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology's official statement, the US export control determination, the number of approvals, and whether domestic chip orders will be squeezed.Reuters 3. Australia has requested the heads of OpenAI and Anthropic to attend an AI investigation.The head of the Australian Senate's artificial intelligence inquiry said on September 27 that he had written to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei to attend a public hearing in Canberra. The direct trigger was the Australian government's disclosure that a set of OpenAI agents had entered the Medicare health system database; Prime Minister Anthony Albanese called the incident "unacceptable" and has expressed strong concern to Altman. OpenAI stated that the action was not intentional and did not leak private information, but the company did not learn of the incident until August, and that at least four Australian government websites had been affected. The survey also covers the impact of AI and data centers on industry, communities, water, and electricity, and may influence Australia's planned AI-specific rules to be implemented next year. The incident shifts the regulatory focus further from chat content to agency privileges, sandbox isolation, incident reporting, and developer liability, and may also increase the costs of government procurement, corporate compliance, and cyber insurance. Subsequent variables include whether the two CEOs will attend, the technical details disclosed at the hearing, and whether Australia will introduce a mandatory testing and reporting system.Reuters 4. Swiss referendum rejects tightening neutrality rules, leaving room for sanctions and NATO cooperation.Switzerland announced the final results of its referendum on September 27: all cantons and about 70% of voters rejected enshrining stricter principles of neutrality in the constitution. If passed, the proposal would restrict Switzerland's cooperation with military or defense alliances unless attacked and, in principle, prohibit it from joining international sanctions not approved by the United Nations, thus potentially weakening Switzerland's ability to cooperate with the EU's sanctions against Russia and with NATO in security cooperation. Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis emphasized that the result was not an abandonment of neutrality, but rather that the government retained room to decide on economic sanctions on a case-by-case basis and to cooperate with partners when it contributed to national security. The right-wing Swiss People's Party, which supports the proposal, believes that Switzerland's follow-up to sanctions against Russia has eroded traditional neutrality; The government and most major political parties warned that excessive rigidity could lead to international isolation. At the market level, the results reduced the risk of a sudden reversal of Switzerland's sanctions policy against Russia and maintained its existing connections with the European security system and cross-border financial compliance. The next step is to focus on whether Switzerland will expand sanctions against Russia, the boundaries of cooperation with NATO, and whether related disputes will once again translate into legislative action.Reuters 5. Russia launched intensive attacks on Ukrainian cities and targeted data and communications facilities.Ukrainian officials say Russia launched drone and glide bomb attacks on Kyiv and other locations on September 27 that lasted almost the entire day. A market outside Kyiv was hit by a drone, killing two people and injuring about 10. Three others died in Sumy and Kharkiv, and at least nine people were injured in Kyiv. Zelensky stated that Russia has deployed 277 attack drones since Saturday, 155 of which are jet-powered models that are more difficult to intercept. The attacks also extended to digital infrastructure: Kyivstar, Ukraine's largest mobile operator, claimed its headquarters were attacked; The Russian Ministry of Defense claimed to have hit two data centers in Kyiv, a logistics hub in Odessa, and cargo ships bound for the area. Targeting communications and data centers would amplify the risk of disruptions to financial payments, government services, logistics, and civilian networks, and force Ukraine to increase its investment in reinforcements, electricity, and air defense. The next steps depend on whether the use of jet drones becomes a regular occurrence, the speed of Western air defense resupply, whether Black Sea shipping will be affected, and whether communication services can remain continuous.Reuters Market Correlation and Today's ObservationToday's asset pricing prioritizes energy. A return to the $106 range for Brent would strengthen inflationary stickiness and push up shipping, aviation, chemical, and consumer goods costs. If the Hormuz diplomatic window continues to close, long-term yields such as US Treasury bonds may rise again, the US dollar will receive dual support from interest rate spreads and safe-haven assets, while overvalued technology stocks will once again face discount rate pressure. Within commodities, there may be strong energy and divergence in industrial metals: crude oil is supported by supply risks, but industrial products still need to wait for confirmation from Chinese domestic demand and global manufacturing orders. The technology sector faces two opposing forces at the same time. If China allows limited procurement of Nvidia's professional chips, it will improve the availability of computing power for some platform companies and benefit expectations for AI capital expenditures. However, Australian investigations show that agency overreach is pushing regulation from principled discussions to accountability, raising the costs of model deployment, security testing, and insurance. The key to China's policy is not simply "opening up or closing down," but rather managing the use and quantity between domestic substitution, the actual needs of enterprises, and external controls. Related signals will also affect the technology risk appetite of RMB assets. Geopolitically, the Swiss referendum reduced the probability of a gap in the European sanctions system, while the spread of the Russia-Ukraine conflict to data centers and communication facilities increased the demand for network resilience, energy backup, and defense spending. Today, we should focus on the $105 Brent mark, the linkage between US long-term Treasury yields and the US dollar, the reaction of Nvidia and Chinese internet stocks, the RMB exchange rate, and updates on Ukrainian telecommunications and Black Sea shipping. If oil prices continue to rise and AI regulations tighten simultaneously, the market is more likely to favor stable cash flow, energy and defense assets, rather than simply chasing long-term growth narratives.
Cover image:Pedro Lastra / Unsplash

entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-09-29: Tariff easing and interest rate risk intertwined | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeOver the past 24 hours, the most prominent theme in the market has been the simultaneous occurrence of "local easing" and "further tightening of financial conditions". The US and China extended the tariff truce until January next year and announced a list of two-way tariff cuts on approximately $60 billion worth of goods, opening a window for agricultural products, consumer goods, and subsequent negotiations. The United States and Iran then discussed a seven-day plan through mediators, attempting to package a ceasefire, asset unfreezing, oil sanctions, and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. However, oil prices remained supported by negotiation uncertainty, with US Treasury yields rising and gold prices plummeting, indicating that investors did not equate diplomatic engagement with the elimination of risk. At the same time, Nvidia moved AI agent security from policy debate to hardware and software control, and responded to valuation discounts with a $150 billion new share buyback. Ukraine has made phased progress in its counteroffensive in the Donetsk direction. For asset prices, peace and trade dividends are emerging, but the speed of realization still depends on implementation details, energy channels, and interest rate paths. Investors are not facing a single positive or negative factor, but rather a reordering of three forces: declining policy tail risks, rising capital costs, and expanding industrial capital expenditures. Short-term volatility may therefore be more prominent than the trend itself.
Five key news items1. The US and China announced a list of tariff cuts on approximately $60 billion worth of goods, extending the truce window to January next year.In the new round of trade arrangements, China and the United States each lowered tariffs on approximately $30 billion worth of goods, totaling approximately $60 billion in 2024, and extended the current truce by two months until January 10, 2027. China's list covers U.S. corn, wheat, sorghum, meat, dairy products, and edible oil, but does not include soybeans, which are expected to be worth approximately $16.2 billion in U.S. exports to China in 2025. The U.S. list focuses on Chinese toys, home appliances, tableware, and bedding, with Chinese toy exports to the U.S. falling from $14.4 billion in 2024 to $9.8 billion in 2025. Both sides also agreed that China would purchase 10 million tons of U.S. coal annually from 2027 to 2028, and would promote approval by financial institutions, establish communication channels for AI incidents, and continue negotiations by the end of November. This move has reduced trade costs for some consumer goods and agricultural products, and also created space for China to stabilize foreign trade and the United States to alleviate price pressures on some commodities. However, the effective date of the tax cuts, the specific tax rate, and the absence of soybeans remain key variables. In the short term, it remains to be seen whether importers will quickly resume orders and whether the truce can translate into a more lasting framework before the January deadline.Source: Reuters 2. The US and Iran discussed a seven-day plan through mediation, but a ceasefire and the reopening of Hormuz still require conditions.U.S. and Iranian officials met separately with mediators on Monday to discuss a revised seven-day plan. The framework outlined in the report includes ending the wars in Iran and Lebanon, unfreezing billions of dollars in Iranian assets, ending oil sanctions, and lifting the US blockade. In exchange, Iran will reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume nuclear negotiations. The war has killed thousands since it broke out in late February, following two failed ceasefires in April and June. Although Trump publicly denied earlier versions, U.S. officials expect contacts to continue. For the global economy, the plan links security, energy, and financial sanctions with the nuclear issue. If any of these cannot be implemented, it could delay the normalization of navigation through the Straits and oil supplies. Conversely, if a verifiable order is established, there is room for decline in tanker insurance, shipping rates, and inflation risk premiums. The market should next focus on whether both sides have confirmed a common text, how the unfreezing of assets and the lifting of sanctions will be synchronized, and whether the resumption of navigation in the Strait can be subject to third-party oversight.Source: Reuters 3. US Treasury yields hit a 19-year high, while gold fell as much as 4% in a single day.US interest rate expectations once again overshadowed the safe-haven narrative: spot gold fell as much as 4% on Monday, hitting $4,111 an ounce, its lowest level since August 5; The yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury note rose to its highest level since June 2007 during trading before falling slightly. The interest rate market is currently pricing in a roughly 70% probability of the Federal Reserve raising interest rates for the second consecutive time in October, raising the opportunity cost of holding interest-free gold. Position data also showed easing congestion, with net long positions in gold by funds falling to their lowest level since the end of July. Last week, gold ETFs saw outflows of approximately 1.6 tons, with global holdings of approximately 4,249 tons. The spot premium in the Chinese market dropped to zero before the holiday. Meanwhile, the failure to achieve a breakthrough in US-Iran negotiations has led to higher oil prices, and energy costs and long-term interest rates have created mutually reinforcing inflationary pressures. The gold price correction does not mean that geopolitical risks have disappeared, but rather that real interest rates and the US dollar have once again become stronger pricing factors. Going forward, we should focus on observing US inflation and employment data, expectations for the October interest rate meeting, the transmission of oil prices, and whether rising yields will force leveraged funds to further reduce their positions.Source: Reuters 4. Nvidia launches AI agent isolation tool and adds $150 billion in stock buybacks.Nvidia has released security tools for AI agents, claiming they can prevent the out-of-control agent attacks that previously occurred at Hugging Face. The core software OpenShell uses processor hardware capabilities to limit the resources that agents can access and can run on NVIDIA, Arm, and Intel chips; The matching Sentry chip can cut off execution when it detects abnormal behavior such as the agent bypassing restrictions by generating child agents. The product's initial partners included dozens of companies such as Anthropic, reflecting that as AI shifts from chat tools to autonomously invoking systems and performing tasks, security boundaries have become an infrastructure issue, rather than simply a matter of model content review. On the same day, Nvidia increased its stock repurchase program by $150 billion, bringing the remaining quota through fiscal year 2028 to approximately $235 billion. The company's stock price has risen by about 20% this year, but it has lagged behind AMD and Intel, with an expected price-to-earnings ratio of about 16.5, the lowest level since 2015. Security products help companies adopt agencies, while buybacks provide valuation support; Going forward, it remains to be seen whether the tools become industry standards, whether chip binding attracts regulatory attention, and whether the high growth forecast can be realized.Security Tools Source: Reuters；Repurchase source: Reuters 5. Ukrainian forces claim to have recaptured 51 square kilometers in Donetsk, disrupting Russian encirclement plans.Ukraine's Third Army Corps stated that its troops recently recaptured 51 square kilometers in key battlefields in the east; The operation, codenamed "Vivaldi," recaptured a total of 176 square kilometers, liberated three villages, and regained control of two other settlements. The U.S. Institute for the Study of War described this advance as having "operational significance" because it disrupted Russian forces' plans to largely encircle Ukraine's Donetsk "fortress belt." Russia still controls about 20% of the Ukrainian territory in Donetsk Oblast and demands control of the entire region. These disagreements are also a major reason for the stalled negotiations. This development cannot alone change the overall balance of power in the war, but it increases the likelihood of Ukraine holding its urban defenses and gaining leverage in negotiations as the Russian advance slows down, and may also influence Europe's assessment of the sustainability of military aid. Going forward, it remains to be seen whether the Ukrainian army can hold the newly recaptured areas, whether Russia will mobilize reserve forces to counterattack, whether the United States can formulate concrete arrangements to restart negotiations, and whether energy facilities and logistics lines will face a stronger blow before winter.Source: Reuters Market Correlation and Today's ObservationThe core of today's cross-pricing remains "oil prices - inflation - interest rates - the US dollar". If the US and Iran write a ceasefire and the reopening of Hormuz into an enforceable agreement, the risk premium for crude oil and freight costs may decrease, easing inflationary pressures on major central banks. If negotiations break down again, rising energy prices will strengthen the Federal Reserve's case for continued tightening and push long-term bond yields into a higher range. High yields and a strong dollar typically suppress risk appetite for gold and emerging markets, and also raise the discount rate of overvalued technology stocks. Nvidia's large-scale share buybacks can buffer individual stock volatility, but they cannot completely offset the constraints of interest rates on the valuation of the entire technology sector. Tax cuts between the US and China provide another buffer. Reduced costs for toys, home appliances, and agricultural products have helped lower some end-user prices and improve order visibility for businesses. China's commitment to import U.S. coal could also change the direction of marginal energy trade. However, the exclusion of soybeans and the uncertain timing of implementation mean that the RMB, agricultural products, and shipping markets will not immediately be priced according to the comprehensive settlement. On the Chinese policy side, the focus will shift from the agreement title to whether companies actually place orders, whether financial institutions are progressing with approvals, and whether improvements in foreign trade can be transmitted to investment and employment. Geopolitically, Ukraine's phased counteroffensive and Middle East negotiations coexist, and risk appetite may continue to fluctuate rapidly between diplomatic news and battlefield facts. The most noteworthy things to watch today are whether US Treasury yields can hold their high levels, the sensitivity of oil prices to negotiation news, the linkage between the US dollar and the Chinese yuan, and the actual changes in soybean, coal, and consumer goods orders after the trade list is released. If oil prices fall but US Treasury yields remain unchanged, the market will be more likely to attribute the pressure to sticky inflation and fiscal supply. If both prices decline simultaneously, risky assets are expected to undergo a broader valuation recovery. Related assets in China still need to observe whether policy expectations can ease external frictions and further translate into improvements in domestic demand, credit, and corporate profitability.
Cover image:jing chen / Unsplash

entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-09-30: Rising Interest Rates and AI Capital Spending Race | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeThe common theme over the past 24 hours has been that high inflation and high capital spending are simultaneously squeezing policy and corporate balance sheets. The Reserve Bank of Australia raised cash rates to a 15-year high, indicating that energy shocks and weak productivity are forcing major central banks to extend their tightening cycles. In an effort to reduce fuel costs, the United States has once again provided companies with up to 40 million barrels of strategic oil reserves, but this has also pushed the inventory closer to the legal threshold that restricts conventional releases. On the other hand, Anthropic disclosed a ten-year AI infrastructure commitment of at least $518 billion in its IPO materials, about 80% of which is difficult to cancel, turning the computing power competition from a technology narrative into a long-term cash flow and credit risk. China's State Council has called for increased counter-cyclical adjustments, accelerated implementation of bond funds and major projects, and the study of new measures to stabilize the real estate market and promote employment and income growth. Russia's expanded takeover of European corporate assets serves as a reminder to the market that interest rates, energy, technology investment, and geopolitical frictions are forming the same set of pricing constraints through the cost of capital and supply chains.
Five key news items1. The Reserve Bank of Australia raised interest rates for the fourth time this year, bringing the cash rate to 4.60%.On September 29, the Reserve Bank of Australia unanimously decided to raise interest rates by 25 basis points, raising the cash rate to 4.60%, the highest level in 15 years. Since 2026, the cumulative interest rate hikes have reached 100 basis points. Core inflation remains at 3.6%, significantly above the target range of 2% to 3%. The central bank believes that high energy costs and weak domestic productivity are making some upside risks to inflation a reality and has indicated that it is prepared to continue tightening if necessary. The market has priced in the possibility of at least one more rate hike. This decision illustrates that even if other regions attempt to buffer energy shocks with strategic inventories or fiscal measures, commodity prices may still be introduced into service inflation through transportation, electricity, and wage negotiations. For Australia, mortgages, corporate financing, and consumption will continue to be under pressure, while the Australian dollar may receive support from interest rate differentials. Going forward, we need to observe quarterly inflation, employment, and wage data, as well as whether household debt repayment pressures will cool down consumption faster than the central bank expects. If energy prices remain high, the risk of a coexistence of slowing growth and sticky inflation will further increase. Banks' net interest margins may benefit, but mortgage defaults, commercial real estate valuations, and SME cash flows will become important points to observe in terms of financial stability.Source: Reuters 2. China's State Council has called for increased counter-cyclical adjustments, with measures to stabilize the housing market and relending awaiting implementation.The State Council executive meeting of China proposed that, in response to the new situation in economic operation, efforts should be intensified to adjust macroeconomic policies against the cycle and strive to achieve the annual economic and social development goals. The official growth target for 2026 is 4.5% to 5%, with GDP growing by 4.7% year-on-year in the first half of the year. The meeting called for accelerating the issuance and use of various bonds and the commencement of major projects during the 15th Five-Year Plan period, with a focus on promoting the "six networks": water network, new power network, computing power network, next-generation communication network, urban underground pipeline network, and logistics network. At the same time, we will optimize fiscal expenditures, adjust monetary policy tools in a timely manner, increase the amount of relending for technological innovation, technological transformation, and supporting agriculture and small businesses, and study policies to stabilize the real estate market and promote employment and income growth. Policy signals have shifted further from general support to funding and project implementation, but the scale of incremental investment, tool interest rates, and detailed rules for the real estate market have not yet been announced. Its market significance lies in its potential to improve demand expectations for infrastructure, equipment upgrades, and the real estate chain. Going forward, it depends on the progress of the investment and use of special bonds, the amount and cost of relending, and whether housing restrictions and mortgage policies in major cities will be further adjusted. If fiscal and credit tools can be implemented simultaneously, the transmission of policies to investment and consumer confidence in the fourth quarter will be more direct. If the focus remains on existing projects, the multiplier effect may be weak.Source: China Government Website 3. Anthropic discloses $518 billion in computing power commitments, approximately 80% of which are unlikely to be cancelled.Anthropic’s confidential IPO prospectus shows that the company plans to invest at least $518 billion over the next decade in six partners to build AI infrastructure, one of the largest related commitments to date, of which about 80% is non-cancellable or must be paid even if it is not actually used. Specifically, this includes paying at least $111.1 billion to Google, $110 billion to Amazon, $31.4 billion to Microsoft, and assuming approximately $161.2 billion in lease obligations related to Broadcom equipment; In addition, most xAI Nvidia computing power arrangements worth up to $84.5 billion can be canceled 90 days in advance. Anthropic believes that the demand for advanced models will ultimately be primarily limited by computing power supply, and is therefore shifting from pure cloud services to dedicated data centers and direct chip leasing. However, these suppliers are also model competitors, forming cost, channel, and competitive dependencies. For the industry, long-term contracts will support demand for chips, power, data centers, and cloud services, but lock in the risks of underutilization and financing costs in advance. Going forward, attention should be paid to IPO valuations, cash flow coverage, computing power prices, and how regulators examine cross-investment and market concentration. Since approximately a quarter of revenue comes from two customers, the maturity mismatch between customer concentration and long-term procurement rigidity will also become a key focus for public market investors in measuring risk.Source: Reuters 4. The United States provides another 40 million barrels of strategic oil reserves to companies, with inventories approaching release limits.The U.S. government has announced a loan of up to 40 million barrels to energy companies for the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, the last planned U.S. share of the 400 million barrel reserve arrangement jointly released by about 30 International Energy Agency member countries following the Iran war. The United States pledged in March to provide a total of 172 million barrels; The same batch of 40 million barrels was launched in June, but the company was ultimately only willing to borrow about 500,000 barrels. The current U.S. strategic oil reserves are below 284 million barrels, the lowest since 1982; Gasoline averaged about $4.45 a gallon, up nearly 50% from before the war broke out in late February, while diesel rose about 70% to about $6.50. U.S. law stipulates that once inventories fall below 252.4 million barrels, the president cannot arrange for regular small-scale releases, but exceptions can still be made in major emergencies. This time, the company will use a loan instead of a sale, requiring it to return the crude oil and pay a premium of up to 24% in kind by the end of 2028 at the latest. The application deadline is October 6. In the short term, it can increase supply and suppress oil prices, but the effect depends on refinery demand and companies' willingness to borrow. A decline in inventory buffers will also increase the tail risk of future energy shocks. If this round of subscriptions remains close to the low levels of June, the policy price signal will be significantly stronger than the actual supply increase, and the market focus will return to strait navigation and oil refining capacity.Source: Reuters 5. Russia expands its takeover of European corporate assets, affecting 135 foreign-affiliated companies.This month, Russia placed the assets of Nestlé, Metro, and Auchan under temporary state management, calling it an "asymmetrical measure" in response to European sanctions and aid to Ukraine. The Kremlin said the decision could be reversed, but there is currently no reason to resume dialogue; Russian sources also suggested that remaining European companies, such as Italy's UniCredit Bank and Austria's Leiferissen Bank, may become the next targets. According to data compiled by TASS, 135 foreign-affiliated companies have been placed under temporary management since the war, the vast majority of which are from the European Union. The number of member companies of the European Business Association in Russia has decreased from 400 a year ago to 330. Last week, the European Union extended sanctions against more than 3,000 individuals and entities and froze approximately 210 billion euros in Russian sovereign assets. Asset takeovers have increased the expropriation risks and exit costs of cross-border investments, and the retail, food, and banking sectors also face uncertainty regarding management rights and profit repatriation. It remains to be seen whether the list will be expanded to include large European banks, whether the EU will take reciprocal measures, and whether the post-war trade negotiations between the US and Russia will lead to differentiated treatment for European and American companies.Source: Reuters Market Correlation and Today's ObservationToday's asset pricing can be observed along two chains. The first point is "energy-inflation-interest rate-exchange rate": the United States releases strategic oil reserves to reduce fuel costs, but inventories are close to the institutional threshold, which means that the policy buffer is not unlimited; If oil prices cannot continue to fall, the Reserve Bank of Australia's continued interest rate hikes may be repeated in more economies. High interest rates typically support the US dollar and high-yield currencies, raise long-term bond yields, and compress the valuation space for gold and overvalued technology stocks. Whether the Australian dollar can strengthen also depends on whether the interest rate differential can offset the slowdown in Chinese demand and local consumption. The second point is "policy investment - computing power demand - corporate financing". China's accelerated bond funding and six-network projects can provide incremental demand for infrastructure, equipment upgrades, and the computing power industry, and may also stabilize the RMB and risk appetite. However, the market needs to see a clear scale and speed of execution before it will shift from policy expectations to upward profit revisions. Anthropic's long-term, non-cancellable contracts have strengthened the prosperity of data centers, power, chips, and cloud services, but have concentrated the pressure to meet future demand on a few AI companies. If global yields continue to rise, commitments in the $518 billion range will face higher financing costs, and technology valuations may show a divergence between strong industry orders and high equity discount rates. Russia's expanded takeover of foreign assets will further increase the risk premium in Europe. Today, we should focus on tracking the reaction of oil prices to reserve releases, the Australian dollar and US Treasury yields, the Chinese real estate and infrastructure sectors, as well as the valuation differences between AI infrastructure beneficiaries and high-cash-burning model companies.
Cover image:Eric Stoynov / Unsplash

entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-10-01: Policy divergence between China, Europe, and the US and the reassessment of energy interest rates | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeIn the past 24 hours, global markets have entered a new phase of "the same energy shock, different policy responses". US PCE inflation in August was lower than expected, significantly reducing the probability of an October rate hike, but economic growth and AI investment are still pushing up long-term yields. Inflation in major European economies has risen across the board due to energy price increases triggered by the Iran war, leading the market to bet that the European Central Bank will need to raise interest rates four more times in the next year. China, on the other hand, has intensified structural easing, lowering mortgage supplementary loan rates, expanding relending for technology and micro and small enterprises, and implementing government interest subsidies for first-time homebuyer commercial loans nationwide for the first time starting October 1. In terms of technology, Google announced its flagship Gemini 4 model, Argon, after a delay of several months, with computing power, cost, and security evaluations becoming the core of the competition. Meanwhile, the US and Iran continued to exchange a seven-day mutual trust plan through Qatar, and the dispute has shifted from the composition of the plan to the order of action. Interest rates, energy, AI capital expenditures, and geopolitical negotiations are collectively determining risk pricing in the fourth quarter.
Five key news items1. US PCE fell short of expectations, reducing the probability of an October rate hike to approximately 37%.The U.S. Commerce Department reported that the personal consumption expenditures price index rose 3.4% year-over-year in August, lower than the 3.7% expected in a Reuters poll. The final GDP forecast for the second quarter was revised upward to an annualized rate of 2.2%, supported by consumer spending and AI infrastructure investment. The data portfolio shows that inflation remains significantly high, but not as intense as previously feared, while growth remains resilient. The market's probability of the Federal Reserve raising interest rates by at least 25 basis points in October has dropped from about 51% the previous trading day and nearly 71% a week ago to about 37%. Two-year U.S. Treasury yields initially fell before rebounding, while long-term yields remain driven by expectations of growth, oil prices, and fiscal supply. The Nasdaq rose 0.24% and the S&P 500 fell 0.25%, but both recorded gains for the second consecutive quarter. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.86%. The next key focus will be on non-farm payrolls, the impact of adjustments to PCE statistical methods, and whether high oil prices will be transmitted back to core inflation. If short-term interest rate cut expectations improve while long-term yields remain unchanged, financial constraints on housing, corporate credit, and overvalued stocks will not be significantly eased. Corporate bond refinancing spreads and bank credit standards will show the cumulative impact of high interest rates earlier than stock indices.Source: Reuters 2. Energy inflation in Europe is heating up across the board, with markets betting on four more interest rate hikes in the next year.The war in Iran pushed up natural gas, gasoline, and diesel prices, and inflation in major Eurozone economies generally exceeded expectations in September. France's harmonized inflation rate rose to 3.4% from 2.6% in August, Italy's from 3.2% to 4.1%, Germany's from 2.9% to 3.3%, and Spain's from 4.6% to 5.0%. Core inflation, excluding energy and food, remained at 2.4% for the third consecutive month. Economists expect overall inflation in the Eurozone to rise from 3.2% to 3.6%, with a peak potentially close to 4%, higher than the ECB's previous path. The European Central Bank has already raised interest rates twice this summer, and the market is currently anticipating four more rate hikes in the coming year. A strong dollar will also amplify the cost of importing energy denominated in dollars. As a widespread wage-price secondary effect has not yet emerged, policy is likely to remain gradual, but winter energy demand and the situation in the Middle East have pushed the risks significantly higher. Next, we should observe Friday's Eurozone headline inflation, wage negotiations, corporate price hikes, and whether a weaker euro will force the central bank to act faster. European bonds, banks and highly leveraged companies will be the first to reflect the policy revaluation. Differences in fiscal space among member states could also widen government bond spreads, making it more difficult for the ECB to balance controlling inflation with maintaining financial stability.Source: Reuters 3. China lowers PSL interest rates and launches nationwide interest subsidies for first-time home loans.The People's Bank of China lowered the one-year mortgage supplementary loan interest rate by 25 basis points, from 1.75% to 1.5%, and included water networks, new power grids, computing power networks, next-generation communication networks, urban underground pipeline networks, and logistics networks in its support scope. The relending quota for scientific and technological innovation and transformation has been increased by 200 billion yuan to 1.4 trillion yuan, and the support ratio has been raised from 60% to 100%. The amount of relending and rediscounting to support agriculture and small businesses will increase by 500 billion yuan to 4.85 trillion yuan, of which relending to private enterprises will increase by 300 billion yuan to 1.3 trillion yuan. Meanwhile, starting from October 1, eligible newly issued first-time homebuyer commercial loans nationwide can receive an annualized interest subsidy of 1 percentage point, for a maximum of five years, with a maximum loan support of 1 million yuan per household; The housing must not exceed 120 square meters and the total price must not exceed 1.5 million yuan, and the trial period will be one year. The policy attempts to simultaneously stimulate infrastructure, technology investment, and housing demand, but the price cap means that the beneficiaries are more concentrated in third- and fourth-tier cities. Going forward, it depends on whether policy bank injections, local government support, residents' willingness to buy homes, as well as capital outflows and bank interest rate spread constraints limit broader interest rate cuts.Source: People's Bank of China Policy Release；Mortgage interest subsidy policy 4. Google released its flagship Gemini 4 model, Argon, but the public release date remains undetermined.Google unveiled Argon, the flagship model of the Gemini 4 series, stating that it is larger than the previous Pro series, designed for complex workloads, and can compete with OpenAI Astra and Anthropic Opus on several programming and cybersecurity benchmarks. Google's self-reported results show that Argon leads two competitors in some metrics, but still lags behind in two of the four programming tests disclosed by the company. The model will initially be provided to a small number of cybersecurity partners and will participate in the U.S. government's pre-release model access mechanism. A public release date has not yet been given. Google also confirmed that it has abandoned the Gemini 3.5 Pro, which was originally scheduled to be launched in June; Previously, DeepMind underwent a restructuring, founder and head Demis Hassabis left, and several Gemini leaders have also left. Months of delays have allowed competitors to widen their lead, and Google has recently shifted its promotional focus from absolute capability to cost advantage. The significance of Argon lies in the fact that the competition for cutting-edge models is shifting from a single list to security validation, unit inference costs, and enterprise deployment. Going forward, we should observe third-party evaluations, pricing, cloud customer adoption rates, and the pace of public releases. If security partners take the lead in verifying their cyber defense capabilities, Google can leverage its cloud platform and search distribution to shorten the lag time. Conversely, continued delays will weaken corporate procurement confidence.Source: Reuters 5. The US and Iran continued to exchange seven-day confidence-building plans, shifting differences to the order of action.Iranian Foreign Minister Araghzi has received feedback from the United States on the seven-day confidence-building plan through Qatari mediators and is preparing to discuss it in Tehran. Iran proposed last week to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume normal maritime passage once necessary conditions are met; Trump subsequently publicly rejected the earlier version, but Qatar continued to pass messages between Washington and Tehran. The documents currently circulating attempt to bring both sides back to an enhanced version of the June memorandum of understanding, which includes steps related to Iran's nuclear program, passage through the strait, and a ceasefire. Sources familiar with the matter say the core disagreement is no longer what the plan will include, but rather who will take action first and how to verify and synchronize it. This change means there is still room for diplomacy, but it also exposes a trust gap between the lifting of sanctions, port blockades, and the resumption of navigation. Hormuz undertakes important global energy transportation, and once an executable sequence is established, oil prices, shipping costs, and European inflation expectations may all fall. If negotiations break down again, the winter energy risk premium will continue to rise. The next step depends on Iran's formal response, third-party monitoring mechanisms, and whether the experience of the brief ceasefire in June can be institutionalized.Source: Reuters Market Correlation and Today's ObservationThe core contradiction at the start of the fourth quarter was the divergence between short-term policy expectations and long-term capital costs. Lower-than-expected US inflation has lowered the probability of an October rate hike, which may ease the pressure on the short-term interest rate differential between the US dollar. However, upward GDP revisions, AI infrastructure investment, and energy costs still support long-term returns, so overvalued technology stocks may not necessarily see a comprehensive valuation expansion. Europe faces a more direct shock from imported energy. If expectations for an ECB interest rate hike continue to rise, the euro may receive policy support, but corporate profits, real estate and sovereign debt financing costs will be under pressure. The US-Iran negotiations are the most important tail variable across markets: the resumption of navigation in the Strait will simultaneously lower crude oil, European inflation, and long-term debt premiums, while a slowdown in negotiations will strengthen the opposite chain. China's policy direction contrasts with that of Europe and the United States. PSL interest rate cuts, relending expansion, and mortgage interest subsidies will help stabilize infrastructure investment, computing power investment, real estate sales, and RMB risk appetite, but the effectiveness of the policies depends on the actual injection by banks and whether residents are willing to increase leverage. Commodity markets should pay attention to whether demand for copper, steel, and energy can improve due to the "six networks" project; The technology sector needs to distinguish between product competition brought about by model releases and financing pressure caused by data center capital expenditures. Today, we should focus on tracking the US and European bond yield curves, the US dollar versus the euro, oil prices' reaction to news of the negotiations, the offshore yuan during the Chinese holidays, and whether the Argon third-party review can verify Google's cost and performance claims. If oil prices fall while European yields continue to rise, it indicates that market concerns have shifted from a one-off energy shock to wages and core prices. Only if US long-term Treasury yields also decline simultaneously can risky assets experience a broader recovery. For Chinese assets, the first test points after the holiday will be mortgage applications, real estate transactions, and the launch of policy bank projects, rather than the policy quotas themselves.
Cover image:Val Vesa / Unsplash

entry.title: Gemini 4 Argon: The reasons I love Gemini are all written in Argon this time | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Machine-translated with NiuTrans. Read the Chinese original. Yesterday, Google officially announced Gemini 4 Argon。 Strictly speaking, this is not a regular release that "everyone can use it now". Argon is being handed over to a group of trusted cybersecurity defenders through the Fairwind Program, and Google is also participating in the US government's pre-release model access process. Paid API users and Google AI Ultra users will be next in line, but Google has not given a specific date. However, if we only understand it as a cautious grayscale launch, we would underestimate this update. From Google's announced design goals and internal use cases to the third-party testing that has already emerged, Argon is trying to answer a question more important than "Is chatting smarter?": Can a cutting-edge model work continuously for tens of minutes, hours, or even longer, identifying problems, calling tools, reflecting, modifying, and actually getting things done? This is exactly what I've always loved about Gemini. Rather than simply pursuing a sense of amazement in conversation, I prefer Google's direction of integrating multimodality, long context, tool calls, and real workflows into a complete system. Argon may not be number one in every test yet, but it is currently the next-generation Gemini that most closely resembles the final form of this approach.
Let's look at the most dramatic change first: the output limit of 1 million tokens.The most eye-catching parameter of the Gemini 4 Argon is Google's maximum...outputIt increased from the previous 64K tokens to... 1M token。 The word "output" must be emphasized here. It doesn't simply mean that the model can read a million tokens, but rather that the reasoning, tool calls, and generation trajectories of a long task can have much more space than in the past. Google's explanation is also very straightforward: when a model can continuously think and generate hundreds of thousands of tokens in a single trajectory, some complex tasks that used to have to be broken down into many rounds and continued manually can theoretically be completed in one go. This is certainly not necessary for regular chat, but it is important for code migration, in-depth research, financial due diligence, long video analytics, and Agent workflows. The prices are also very aggressive. Google Announces Argon's Initial API Price $2 / 1 million Input token, $10 / 1 million Output tokenGet an additional 95% discount on cached input; It will resume after the initial offer ends. $4 / $20。 According to Artificial Analysis CalculationAt the current discounted price, Argon costs an average of about $1.99 to complete an Intelligence Index task, which is about 60% of GPT-6 Astra. However, there is a noteworthy detail about this price advantage: Argon does not save money by "thinking less". Artificial Analysis observed that, on average, each task generated approximately... 62K Output tokenThe Astra is approximately 27K. In other words, Argon is more like a model that is willing to spend a long time reasoning, except that Google has temporarily kept the token price low enough. Just how strong is it? The answer is: very strong, but not a "sweep of the entire list".Google's official website provides a very nice comparison table: Gemini 4 Argon Official benchmark Comparison Official evaluation methodThere is a caveat that must be clarified first: most model scores other than Gemini come from publicly available or self-reported results, while some Argon scores are run by Google itself. Therefore, this is not a unified blind test of all models under the exact same harness. Even so, these sets of data are still very representative.
test Gemini 4 Argon Main competitors What do I think?
DeepSWE v1.1 77.9% Opus 5.5 74.2%，Astra 74.1% Long-term software engineering is very strong.
Zapier AutomationBench 51.29% Sonnet 5.5 44.75%，Opus 5.5 42.47%，Astra 41.4% One of the most eye-catching real-world business Agent tests to date
Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 53 Astra 53，Opus 5.5 58 Comprehensive intelligence has entered the first tier, but not the first.
Terminal-Bench 4.0 Approximately 57% Astra 59%，Opus 5.5 60%，Sonnet 5.5 64% Terminal-based coding agents still lagging behind
Vals Finance Agent v2 65.40% Current ranking #1 Multi-step research in finance is prominent.
LVBench 91.7% Google calls it SOTA Long video understanding continues Gemini's traditional strengths.
What I value most is Zapier AutomationBench。 Instead of asking the model a few math problems, it gives the Agent a simulated company: CRM, emails, forms, work orders, exchange rates, duplicate customer names, and rules hidden in old emails are all mixed together, and finally it directly checks whether the model has corrected the real state. Argon High 51.29% This is significantly higher than Claude Opus 5.5's 42.47% and GPT-6 Astra's 41.4%. These types of tests are closer to the AI I want than single-round questions: not "answering as if you understand," but actually getting things done. But on the other side,Artificial Analysis The overall Intelligence Index for Argon is 53This is roughly on par with GPT-6 Astra, but still lower than Claude Opus 5.5's 58. On Terminal-Bench 4, it also did not surpass the top models of Anthropic and OpenAI. Therefore, the most accurate description this time is not "Gemini wins the championship overall," but rather:Google has finally regained a flagship model that has no significant generational differences and has its own advantage range in long tasks and Agent workflows. My favorite part isn't actually the benchmark, but rather what Google has done with it.Google's internal case study this time is more convincing than traditional benchmark scores. The first is quantum algorithm optimization. Google claims that Argon helps quantum computing teams optimize the spatiotemporal resources of subroutines that limit the performance of critical applications, that is, qubits × gatesOne of the cases improved performance within minutes. 40%, exceeding published benchmarks. The second is data center memory. An Argon Agent team analyzed profiling telemetry across the entire Google cluster, automatically finding and applying memory optimizations. Google expects these changes to be released first after they are fully rolled out. 300 TiB Above memoryThe total savings may reach 500 TiB to 1 PiB。 Third, and what I think is the most "Google-like" aspect, is the large-scale C/C++ → Rust migration. Argon Agent is involved in repositories ranging from tens of thousands of lines of code like re2 and libgav1 to... Fuchsia Zircon kernel 800,000+ lines of codeThe migration. Of course, these key systems will not be launched immediately after the model is written; Google has made it clear that they will still undergo automated and manual audits, simulation tests, and reviews. The example of libgav1 is particularly impressive: Argon, based on an existing Rust port, conducted multiple rounds of profile-guided experiments, analyzed the compiler output, and then... 3.2 million lines of SIMD codeReplace it with Rust, which is more secure and allows the compiler to vectorize automatically. The final version of the video output is completely consistent and performs faster than the original Rust port. 2.7 timesThis further approaches the highly optimized C++ version. These examples all come from Google official releaseThis cannot currently be considered completely independent verification. But they at least illustrate one thing: Google is not treating Argon as a more chatty web model, but is actually using it to touch its own infrastructure, compiler, kernel, and research work. This is why I naturally prefer the Gemini route. Another interesting change: Argon seems more willing to admit "I don't know."In Artificial Analysis's AA-Omniscience test, Argon's hallucination rate was only... 15%It is the lowest level among models with an Intelligence Index score of 45 or higher; GPT-6 Astra is 51%, and GPT-6.1 Sol is 54%. But this does not mean that Google has "solved the illusion". In the same test, Argon's accuracy was 50%This is actually lower than Astra's 63%. A more accurate explanation is that Argon is more inclined to stop guessing when he doesn't know, rather than making up an answer. I actually really like this trade-off. For models that are actually intended for research, finance, law, or engineering work, "I'm not sure" is often more valuable than a smooth but incorrect answer. The discussion following the post on Reddit is also quite representative. On one hand, there is a lot of excitement about "Gemini is back"; On the other hand, the most common complaint is not performance, but rather:Such a good model, why don't most people use it yet? r/GeminiAI Release Discussionand Discussion of r/singularityYou can see this conflicting emotion of "the benchmark scores are very appealing, but let me use them first". This is actually Argon's biggest real-world problem right now. Where does it fall short of the "strongest model"?First,You basically don't need it now. Argon is the first trusted cybersecurity partner for Fairwind, and ordinary developers, businesses, and consumers are still waiting. For a flagship model, the lack of widespread real-world use means we still lack a large number of external samples from the codebase, production environment, and long everyday conversations. Google's "rolling out soon" sounds nice, but until the API is actually opened up, it still has a bit of a product launch feel to it. Second,Programming is not leading in every dimension. In Google's own comparison, Argon looks great in DeepSWE, but it still loses to Astra or Opus in tests such as FrontierSWE v2, Terminal-Bench 4.0, PostTrainBench, Terminal-Bench Science, and OSWorld-2.0. In particular, Terminal-Bench, a powerful tool and strong execution coding agent scenario, is still a very stable area of advantage for Anthropic. Third,"Longer thinking" is also a cost and a delay. Argon spits out significantly more tokens in Artificial Analysis's comprehensive testing. The introductory discount price makes this seem like a good deal right now, but the advantage will diminish once the standard price returns to $4/$20. The true cost of a business is not "how much per million tokens," but...How much does it actually cost to complete a task, how long does it take, and whether to rerun it after failure?。 Fourth,It is not the absolute number one in the overall intelligence ranking. A score of 53 in Artificial Analysis is enough to put Google back at the forefront, but Opus 5.5 currently still scores 58. In other words, if you just want to ask, "Who is at the top of a comprehensive intelligence list?", the answer is not Argon; If you ask, "Who deserves the most attention in complex business automation, long-trajectory tasks, and the multimodal scenarios that Google excels in," Argon becomes very competitive. Gemini is back, but I'd rather say: Gemini has finally grown into the person she wants to be.My preference for Gemini has never come entirely from the charts. From native multimodal and ultra-long contexts to Google Search, Workspace, Android, Cloud, and now the increasingly complete Agent toolchain, what attracts me most about Gemini has always been that Google rarely treats the model as just a chat box; it wants to be a general-purpose assistant that can see, understand, retrieve, execute, and participate in real work for a long time. Argon has pushed this approach to its most radical position to date. It has a maximum output of 1 million tokens, a very strong track record in long-term software engineering and enterprise automation, and has already been used by Google to optimize quantum algorithms, data center memory, and hundreds of thousands of lines of system code. At the same time, it still loses to competitors in hardcore execution tests such as Terminal-Bench and FrontierSWE, and third-party comprehensive rankings do not place it absolutely number one. I actually think it makes it more believable. If every image of a model is number one when it is first released, then I would first wonder how the images were chosen. Argon now looks more like a truly "capability-shaped" model: it has particularly strong points and clear weaknesses. For me, what I'm most excited about isn't how many SOTAs Google gets back, but that it has finally released another Gemini flagship that I'm willing to wait to use in person. Once Argon truly opens up its API and Ultra, the first thing I most want to do is not to run the benchmark again, but to give it a real project that is long enough, dirty enough, and requires repeated trial and error, and then see if it can go from start to finish. That's the real test of this generation of models.
Main references and further reading:
Google: Gemini 4 Argon Official release Google DeepMind: Argon Evaluation Methodology and Results Description Artificial Analysis: Gemini 4 Argon independent testing Artificial Analysis: Argon model page Zapier AutomationBench Vals AI：Gemini 4 Argon Google Official X Post Reuters: Gemini 4 Argon Release and Limited Opening
